source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 1 Kings 4:21–34 binds Hebrew 5:1–14; public 5:1–18 binds Hebrew 5:15–32. Other selected records bind matching labels, including 18:33–34 and 20:2–3 original clause boundaries. Exact original XML and all notes are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Introduces the approaching death and direct charge without archaic timing.
verses.before: As David’s days drew near for him to die, he commanded Solomon his son, saying,
verses.after: As David’s death drew near, he gave his son Solomon these instructions:
verses.tsw_comparator: As David’s days drew near for him to die, he commanded Solomon his son, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the death image and gendered exhortation rather than generalizing it.
verses.before: “I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man.
verses.after: “I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong. Show yourself a man.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the charge while retaining its four terms and wisdom/success connection.
verses.before: Keep the charge of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes, his commandments, his judgments, and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may act wisely in all that you do and wherever you turn,
verses.after: Keep the charge of the LORD your God: walk in his ways and keep his statutes, commands, judgments, and testimonies, as written in the law of Moses. Then you may act wisely in everything you do and wherever you turn,
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep the charge of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes, his commandments, his judgments, and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may act wisely in all that you do and wherever you turn,

verses.rationale: Keeps the dynastic promise conditional and the whole-person expression.
verses.before: so that the LORD may establish his word that he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your children keep their way, walking before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their life, you will not lack a man upon the throne of Israel.’
verses.after: and the LORD may fulfill what he promised me: ‘If your sons watch their ways and walk faithfully before me with all their heart and all their being, you will never lack a man on Israel’s throne.’
verses.tsw_comparator: so that the LORD may establish his word that he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your children keep their way, walking before me in faithfulness with all their heart and with all their life, you will not lack a man upon the throne of Israel.’

verses.rationale: Retains David’s account of bloodguilt and its concrete clothing images.
verses.before: “Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s armies, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether: he killed them, shedding the blood of war in peace, and putting the blood of war on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.
verses.after: “You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, shedding the blood of war in peacetime and putting that blood on the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s armies, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether: he killed them, shedding the blood of war in peace, and putting the blood of war on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threatening wisdom charge and Sheol image.
verses.before: Act, then, according to your wisdom; do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.
verses.after: Use your wisdom. Do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Act, then, according to your wisdom; do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.

verses.rationale: Makes the table obligation and past support audible.
verses.before: “But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among people who eat at your table, for they came near to me when I fled from your brother Absalom.
verses.after: But show steadfast love to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite. Let them eat at your table, because they stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they came near to me when I fled from your brother Absalom.

verses.rationale: Keeps David’s oath beside his recollection of the curse.
verses.before: “And look, with you is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim; but he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, ‘I will not put you to death by the sword.’
verses.after: “You also have with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me bitterly when I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, ‘I will not put you to death with the sword.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “And look, with you is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim; but he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, ‘I will not put you to death by the sword.’

verses.rationale: Does not soften David’s command or explain away its tension with the oath.
verses.before: Now do not hold him innocent, for you are a wise man. You will know what you must do to him, and you will bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.”
verses.after: Now do not leave him unpunished. You are a wise man; you will know what to do with him. Bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now do not hold him innocent, for you are a wise man. You will know what you must do to him, and you will bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.”

verses.rationale: Retains the ancestral death idiom with the burial place.
verses.before: Then David lay down with his ancestors, and he was buried in the city of David.
verses.after: David lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then David lay down with his ancestors, and he was buried in the city of David.

verses.rationale: Preserves this passage’s counts without importing the extra months from Samuel.
verses.before: The days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: He had ruled Israel for forty years: seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: The days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains throne succession and emphatic establishment.
verses.before: Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.
verses.after: Solomon took his seat on his father David’s throne, and his kingship became firmly established.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the speakers while retaining the peace repetition.
verses.before: Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother. She said, “Do you come in peace?” And he said, “In peace.”
verses.after: Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother. “Do you come in peace?” she asked. “In peace,” he replied.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother. She said, “Do you come in peace?” And he said, “In peace.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the brief invitation as dialogue.
verses.before: Then he said, “I have something to say to you.” She said, “Speak.”
verses.after: He said, “I have something to say to you.” “Speak,” she said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “I have something to say to you.” She said, “Speak.”

verses.rationale: Leaves Adonijah’s claim attributed to him, not endorsed by the narrator.
verses.before: He said, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel had set their faces toward me to make me king. But the kingdom turned and became my brother’s, for it came to him from the LORD.
verses.after: “You know the kingship was mine,” he said. “All Israel looked to me to be king. But the kingship turned away from me and went to my brother, because it came to him from the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel had set their faces toward me to make me king. But the kingdom turned and became my brother’s, for it came to him from the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses an idiomatic refusal expression while preserving the request sequence.
verses.before: Now I ask one request of you; do not turn away from me.” She said to him, “Speak.”
verses.after: Now I have one request. Do not turn me away.” “Speak,” she told him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I ask one request of you; do not turn away from me.” She said to him, “Speak.”

verses.rationale: Retains Abishag’s identity and the expected maternal influence.
verses.before: He said, “Please speak to King Solomon, for he will not turn away from you, that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.”
verses.after: “Please ask King Solomon to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife. He will not turn you away.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Please speak to King Solomon, for he will not turn away from you, that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.”

verses.rationale: Makes her agreement explicit without assigning a motive.
verses.before: Bathsheba said, “Very well. I will speak to the king for you.”
verses.after: “Very well,” Bathsheba said. “I will speak to the king for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Bathsheba said, “Very well. I will speak to the king for you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves her throne and royal honor rather than reducing it to a casual chair.
verses.before: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat on his throne, and a throne was set for the king’s mother; and she sat at his right hand.
verses.after: Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed to her. Then he sat on his throne and had a throne placed for the king’s mother. She sat at his right.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat on his throne, and a throne was set for the king’s mother; and she sat at his right hand.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated assurance before its reversal.
verses.before: She said, “I ask one small request of you; do not turn away from me.” The king said to her, “Ask, my mother, for I will not turn away from you.”
verses.after: “I have one small request,” she said. “Do not turn me away.” The king answered, “Ask, Mother. I will not turn you away.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She said, “I ask one small request of you; do not turn away from me.” The king said to her, “Ask, my mother, for I will not turn away from you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the request and kinship clear.
verses.before: She said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as a wife.”
verses.after: She said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as a wife.”

verses.rationale: Retains the abrupt expanded accusation rather than inventing a narrated conspiracy.
verses.before: King Solomon answered and said to his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him too! For he is my older brother—and for him, for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”
verses.after: King Solomon answered his mother, “Why ask for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for the kingship for him too! He is my older brother—for him, for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon answered and said to his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him too! For he is my older brother—and for him, for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the self-curse and lethal interpretation of the request.
verses.before: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, “May God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word against his own life.
verses.after: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, “May God do this to me, and more besides, if Adonijah has not spoken these words at the cost of his life!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, “May God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word against his own life.

verses.rationale: Retains house as dynastic imagery and the immediate death sentence.
verses.before: Now, as the LORD lives, who has established me and seated me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house as he spoke, Adonijah will be put to death today.”
verses.after: As the LORD lives—the one who established me, seated me on my father David’s throne, and made me a house as he promised—Adonijah will be put to death today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now, as the LORD lives, who has established me and seated me on the throne of David my father, and who has made me a house as he spoke, Adonijah shall be put to death today.”

verses.rationale: Names the victim and makes the execution explicit.
verses.before: So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.
verses.after: King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck Adonijah down and killed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated reasons for sparing him and the today qualification.
verses.before: To Abiathar the priest the king said, “Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you are a man deserving death. But I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you shared in all that my father suffered.”
verses.after: To Abiathar the priest the king said, “Go to your fields at Anathoth. You deserve death, but I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David and shared all my father’s hardships.”
verses.tsw_comparator: To Abiathar the priest the king said, “Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you are a man deserving death. But I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you shared in all that my father suffered.”

verses.rationale: Connects removal with the narrator’s fulfillment statement.
verses.before: So Solomon drove Abiathar out from being priest to the LORD, fulfilling the word of the LORD that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli at Shiloh.
verses.after: So Solomon removed Abiathar from serving as the LORD’s priest, fulfilling the word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh about Eli’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Solomon drove Abiathar out from being priest to the LORD, fulfilling the word of the LORD that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli at Shiloh.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned Absalom reading and explains the parenthetical chronology.
verses.before: The report came to Joab, for Joab had followed Adonijah, though he had not followed Absalom. So Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
verses.after: When the news reached Joab, he fled to the LORD’s tent and took hold of the altar’s horns. Joab had sided with Adonijah, though he had not sided with Absalom.
verses.tsw_comparator: The report came to Joab, for Joab had followed Adonijah, though he had not followed Absalom. So Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the report from the execution order.
verses.before: It was told King Solomon, “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD, and look, he is beside the altar.” So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, strike him down.”
verses.after: King Solomon was told, “Joab has fled to the LORD’s tent. He is there beside the altar.” Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with the order, “Go, strike him down.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told King Solomon, “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD, and look, he is beside the altar.” So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, strike him down.”

verses.rationale: Names Joab for dialogue clarity and retains the refusal and report.
verses.before: Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, “Thus says the king: ‘Come out.’” But he said, “No. I will die here.” So Benaiah brought the king word, saying, “This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me.”
verses.after: Benaiah went to the LORD’s tent and said to Joab, “The king says, ‘Come out.’” Joab answered, “No. I will die here.” Benaiah went back to the king and reported what Joab had said and how he had answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, “Thus says the king: ‘Come out.’” But he said, “No. I will die here.” So Benaiah brought the king word, saying, “This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me.”

verses.rationale: Makes bloodguilt understandable without endorsing Solomon’s reasoning.
verses.before: The king said to him, “Do as he has said: strike him down and bury him. Remove from me and from my father’s house the blood shed without cause by Joab.
verses.after: The king told him, “Do as he says. Strike him down and bury him. Remove from me and my father’s house the guilt of the blood Joab shed without cause.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to him, “Do as he has said: strike him down and bury him. Remove from me and from my father’s house the blood shed without cause by Joab.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comparison, claimed ignorance and distinct commands.
verses.before: May the LORD return his blood upon his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he, killing them with the sword while my father David did not know it: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.
verses.after: The LORD will bring his blood back on his own head. He struck down two men more righteous and better than he was, killing them with the sword without my father David’s knowledge: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD return his blood upon his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he, killing them with the sword while my father David did not know it: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.

verses.rationale: Retains the contrasting perpetual wishes and blood image.
verses.before: May their blood return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his offspring forever. But for David, for his offspring, for his house, and for his throne, may there be peace from the LORD forever.”
verses.after: May their blood come back on Joab’s head and on his descendants’ heads forever. But may David, his descendants, his house, and his throne have peace from the LORD forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May their blood return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his offspring forever. But for David, for his offspring, for his house, and for his throne, may there be peace from the LORD forever.”

verses.rationale: Keeps death, burial and wilderness location explicit.
verses.before: Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck him down, and put him to death; and he was buried at his house in the wilderness.
verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck Joab down, and killed him. Joab was buried at his own house in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck him down, and put him to death; and he was buried at his house in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Makes the two replacements parallel and clear.
verses.before: The king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab’s place, and the king appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.
verses.after: The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab’s place, and he put Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in Joab’s place, and the king appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive restriction before the named boundary.
verses.before: Then the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go out from there anywhere.
verses.after: Then the king summoned Shimei. “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there,” he said. “Do not leave it to go anywhere else.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go out from there anywhere.

verses.rationale: Preserves the particular crossing and blood-responsibility formula.
verses.before: For on the day you go out and cross the Wadi Kidron, know for certain that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.”
verses.after: Know this: on the day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you will certainly die. Your blood will be on your own head.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For on the day you go out and cross the Wadi Kidron, know for certain that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.”

verses.rationale: Keeps submission and elapsed residence without implying consent is free.
verses.before: Shimei said to the king, “The word is good. As my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.
verses.after: Shimei answered the king, “Your word is good. Your servant will do as my lord the king has said.” Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shimei said to the king, “The word is good. As my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.

verses.rationale: Makes enslaved status and flight explicit; retains names and interval.
verses.before: But after three years, two of Shimei’s servants ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And Shimei was told, “Look, your servants are in Gath.”
verses.after: After three years, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, “Your slaves are in Gath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But after three years, two of Shimei’s servants ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And Shimei was told, “Look, your servants are in Gath.”

verses.rationale: Retains the pursuit and forced return without euphemism.
verses.before: Then Shimei arose, saddled his donkey, and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
verses.after: Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to look for his slaves. He went and brought them back from Gath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Shimei arose, saddled his donkey, and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reported journey distinct from the Kidron wording.
verses.before: Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.
verses.after: Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and returned.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.

verses.rationale: Preserves Solomon’s retelling without harmonizing it into the earlier speech.
verses.before: So the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, saying, ‘On the day you go out and go anywhere, know for certain that you will die’? And you said to me, ‘The word I have heard is good.’
verses.after: The king summoned Shimei and said, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, ‘Know this: on the day you leave and go anywhere else, you will certainly die’? And you told me, ‘Your word is good. I will obey.’
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king sent and called for Shimei, and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, saying, ‘On the day you go out and go anywhere, know for certain that you will die’? And you said to me, ‘The word I have heard is good.’

verses.rationale: Keeps oath and royal command as separate grounds.
verses.before: Why, then, have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the commandment that I commanded you?”
verses.after: Why, then, have you failed to keep your oath by the LORD and the command I gave you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Why, then, have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the commandment that I commanded you?”

verses.rationale: Retains Solomon’s accusation and returning-evil image.
verses.before: The king said to Shimei, “You know all the evil that your heart knows, which you did to David my father. The LORD will return your evil upon your own head.
verses.after: The king also said, “You know in your heart all the evil you did to my father David. The LORD will bring your evil back on your own head.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to Shimei, “You know all the evil that your heart knows, which you did to David my father. The LORD will return your evil upon your own head.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king’s third-person self-reference within his speech.
verses.before: Yet King Solomon will be blessed, and the throne of David will be established before the LORD forever.”
verses.after: But King Solomon will be blessed, and David’s throne will stand firm before the LORD forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But King Solomon will be blessed, and the throne of David will be established before the LORD forever.”

verses.rationale: Names the victim and leaves the execution beside the establishment statement.
verses.before: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. And the kingdom was established in Solomon’s hand.
verses.after: Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He went out, struck Shimei down, and killed him. The kingdom was firmly in Solomon’s hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. And the kingdom was established in Solomon’s hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the marriage alliance and three construction projects together.
verses.before: Solomon made an alliance by marriage with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh’s daughter and brought her into the city of David, until he had finished building his own house, the house of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem.
verses.after: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He married Pharaoh’s daughter and brought her to the City of David until he finished building his own house, the LORD’s house, and the wall around Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon made an alliance by marriage with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh’s daughter and brought her into the city of David, until he had finished building his own house, the house of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s qualification and Name language.
verses.before: Yet the people were sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the LORD in those days.
verses.after: The people were still sacrificing at the high places, because no house for the LORD’s name had yet been built.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the people were sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the LORD in those days.

verses.rationale: Keeps love and the qualified worship practice together without resolving the tension.
verses.before: Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father; only, he was sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.
verses.after: Solomon loved the LORD and followed the statutes of his father David. Still, he sacrificed and burned offerings at the high places.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father; only, he was sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.

verses.rationale: Preserves the location, status and sacrificial number.
verses.before: The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
verses.after: The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice, because it was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.

verses.rationale: Retains both divine designations and the open invitation.
verses.before: At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said, “Ask what I should give you.”
verses.after: At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at night. God said, “Ask what I should give you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said, “Ask what I should give you.”

verses.rationale: Retains repeated steadfast love and the threefold description of David.
verses.before: Solomon said, “You have shown great steadfast love to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with you. You have kept for him this great steadfast love and have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is today.
verses.after: Solomon answered, “You showed great steadfast love to your servant, my father David, because he walked before you in faithfulness, righteousness, and an upright heart toward you. You have kept this great steadfast love for him by giving him a son to sit on his throne today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon said, “You have shown great steadfast love to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with you. You have kept for him this great steadfast love and have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is today.

verses.rationale: Keeps Solomon’s self-description and leadership idiom rather than assigning an age.
verses.before: “Now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father. But I am a small youth; I do not know how to go out or come in.
verses.after: Now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David. But I am only a young boy; I do not know how to go out or come in.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father. But I am a small youth; I do not know how to go out or come in.

verses.rationale: Retains election and the paired counting expressions.
verses.before: “Your servant is among your people, whom you have chosen—a great people, too many to be counted or numbered because of their multitude.
verses.after: Your servant stands among the people you chose, a people so numerous they cannot be counted or numbered.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Your servant is in the midst of your people, whom you have chosen—a great people, too many to be counted or numbered because of their multitude.

verses.rationale: Retains the listening-heart image at the center of wisdom.
verses.before: “Give your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil. For who can judge this weighty people of yours?”
verses.after: Give your servant a listening heart to judge your people and distinguish good from evil. For who can judge this great people of yours?”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Give your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this weighty people of yours?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the evaluation and its stated reason.
verses.before: The matter pleased the Lord, because Solomon had asked for this.
verses.after: The request pleased the Lord: this was what Solomon had asked for.
verses.tsw_comparator: The matter pleased the Lord, because Solomon had asked for this.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three alternatives and judicial hearing sense.
verses.before: God said to him, “Because you have asked for this and have not asked for yourself long life, or asked for yourself riches, or asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment,
verses.after: God said to him, “Because you asked for this, and did not ask for a long life, riches, or the lives of your enemies, but asked for discernment to hear a case justly,
verses.tsw_comparator: God said to him, “Because you have asked for this and have not asked for yourself long life, or asked for yourself riches, or asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment,

verses.rationale: Retains the heart and both temporal comparisons.
verses.before: look, I have done according to your words. Look, I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that none like you has been before you, and none like you will arise after you.
verses.after: I will do as you asked. I give you a wise and discerning heart. No one like you has come before you, and no one like you will arise after you.
verses.tsw_comparator: behold, I have done according to your words. Behold, I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that none like you has been before you, and none like you shall arise after you.

verses.rationale: Keeps unrequested gifts distinct from the conditional life extension.
verses.before: “I have also given you what you did not ask for: both riches and honor, so that no one among kings will be like you all your days.
verses.after: I also give you what you did not ask for: both riches and honor. Among the kings, no one will be like you throughout your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have also given you what you did not ask for: both riches and honor, so that no one among kings shall be like you all your days.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit condition rather than promising longevity unconditionally.
verses.before: “And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.”
verses.after: And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and commands as your father David did, I will lengthen your life.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the awakening, covenant ark, two offerings and feast in sequence.
verses.before: Then Solomon awoke, and look, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. He offered burnt offerings and made well-being offerings, and he made a feast for all his servants.
verses.after: Solomon woke up. It had been a dream. He went to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the Lord’s covenant. He offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, then gave a feast for all his servants.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. He offered burnt offerings and made well-being offerings, and he made a feast for all his servants.

verses.rationale: Retains the women’s stated occupation without adding moral judgment.
verses.before: Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
verses.after: Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the shared dwelling and first speaker’s account.
verses.before: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in one house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.
verses.after: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house. I gave birth while she was there with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in one house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.

verses.rationale: Retains the third day and the emphatic absence of witnesses.
verses.before: “On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together; there was no stranger with us in the house. Only the two of us were in the house.
verses.after: On the third day after I gave birth, she gave birth too. We were alone; no one else was in the house. Just the two of us.
verses.tsw_comparator: “On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together; there was no stranger with us in the house. Only the two of us were in the house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the death’s explanation inside the woman’s testimony.
verses.before: “This woman’s son died in the night, because she lay on him.
verses.after: During the night this woman’s son died because she lay on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This woman’s son died in the night, because she lay on him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the claimed exchange and breast imagery.
verses.before: “She rose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant was sleeping. She laid him in her bosom, and she laid her dead son in my bosom.
verses.after: She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant was asleep. She laid him at her breast and laid her dead son at mine.
verses.tsw_comparator: “She rose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant was sleeping. She laid him in her bosom, and she laid her dead son in my bosom.

verses.rationale: Keeps discovery and recognition distinct.
verses.before: “When I rose in the morning to nurse my son, look, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, look, he was not my son whom I had borne.”
verses.after: When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, he was dead! But when I looked closely at him in the morning, he was not the son I had borne.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “When I rose in the morning to nurse my son, behold, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, behold, he was not my son whom I had borne.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the reversed claims and makes the two speakers trackable.
verses.before: But the other woman said, “No! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.” And this woman said, “No! Your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.” So they spoke before the king.
verses.after: The other woman said, “No! The living son is mine, and the dead one is yours.” The first said, “No! The dead son is yours, and the living one is mine.” So they argued before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the other woman said, “No! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.” And this woman said, “No! Your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.” So they spoke before the king.

verses.rationale: Retains the king’s full repetition instead of summarizing the dispute.
verses.before: Then the king said, “This one says, ‘My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one’; and that one says, ‘No! Your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’”
verses.after: The king said, “This one says, ‘The living son is mine, and the dead one is yours.’ And that one says, ‘No! The dead son is yours, and the living one is mine.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king said, “This one says, ‘My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one’; and that one says, ‘No! Your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the ominous instruction and response unembellished.
verses.before: The king said, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought the sword before the king.
verses.after: Then the king said, “Bring me a sword.” They brought a sword before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought the sword before the king.

verses.rationale: Does not soften the violent order.
verses.before: Then the king said, “Cut the living child in two, and give half to one woman and half to the other.”
verses.after: “Cut the living child in two,” the king said. “Give half to one and half to the other.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king said, “Cut the living child in two, and give half to one woman and half to the other.”

verses.rationale: Makes maternal compassion and emphatic plea audible, retaining the opposing demand.
verses.before: Then the woman whose son was living spoke to the king, because her compassion was stirred for her son. She said, “Please, my lord, give her the living child; by no means put him to death.” But the other said, “He will be neither mine nor yours; cut him in two.”
verses.after: The woman whose son was alive was overwhelmed with compassion for him. She said to the king, “Please, my lord, give her the living child! Whatever you do, do not kill him!” But the other said, “He will belong to neither of us. Cut him in two.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the woman whose son was living spoke to the king, because her compassion was stirred for her son. She said, “Please, my lord, give her the living child; by no means put him to death.” But the other said, “He shall be neither mine nor yours; cut him in two.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the pronoun’s referent from the contrasted pleas.
verses.before: Then the king answered and said, “Give her the living child, and by no means put him to death. She is his mother.”
verses.after: The king answered, “Give the living child to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is his mother.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king answered and said, “Give her the living child, and by no means put him to death. She is his mother.”

verses.rationale: Connects the judgment with public recognition of divine wisdom.
verses.before: All Israel heard the judgment that the king had given, and they stood in awe of the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to do justice.
verses.after: All Israel heard about the judgment the king had given. They stood in awe of him, because they saw that God’s wisdom was in him to do justice.
verses.tsw_comparator: All Israel heard the judgment that the king had given, and they stood in awe of the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to do justice.

verses.rationale: Retains all Israel as the administration’s scope.
verses.before: King Solomon was king over all Israel.
verses.after: King Solomon ruled over all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon was king over all Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps priest in the official roster with its syntactic ambiguity noted.
verses.before: These were the officials he had: Azariah son of Zadok the priest;
verses.after: These were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
verses.tsw_comparator: These were the officials he had: Azariah son of Zadok the priest;

verses.rationale: Preserves both scribes, their shared father and the distinct recorder.
verses.before: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder;
verses.after: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder;
verses.tsw_comparator: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder;

verses.rationale: Retains Abiathar in the roster despite the preceding removal narrative.
verses.before: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
verses.tsw_comparator: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;

verses.rationale: Keeps priest and king’s friend as stated offices rather than flattening both to adviser.
verses.before: Azariah son of Nathan, over the governors; and Zabud son of Nathan, priest and the king’s friend;
verses.after: Azariah son of Nathan, over the district officials; Zabud son of Nathan, priest and the king’s friend;
verses.tsw_comparator: Azariah son of Nathan, over the governors; and Zabud son of Nathan, priest and the king’s friend;

verses.rationale: Makes the coerced labor office explicit.
verses.before: Ahishar, over the household; and Adoniram son of Abda, over the forced labor.
verses.after: Ahishar, over the royal household; Adoniram son of Abda, over the forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahishar, over the household; and Adoniram son of Abda, over the forced labor.

verses.rationale: Explains the rotating provision without losing the number.
verses.before: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household. Each one was responsible for providing for one month in the year.
verses.after: Solomon had twelve district officials over all Israel. They supplied the king and his household, each responsible for one month of the year.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household. Each one was responsible for providing for one month in the year.

verses.rationale: Preserves the patronymic-style name and first district.
verses.before: These were their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
verses.after: Their names were: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
verses.tsw_comparator: These were their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;

verses.rationale: Retains all four district names.
verses.before: Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
verses.after: Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;

verses.rationale: Makes the dependent territories readable.
verses.before: Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth; he had Sokoh and all the land of Hepher;
verses.after: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth, with Socoh and all the land of Hepher under him;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth; he had Sokoh and all the land of Hepher;

verses.rationale: Retains the district and marriage connection.
verses.before: Ben-Abinadab, over all the district of Dor; Taphath, Solomon’s daughter, was his wife;
verses.after: Ben-abinadab, over all the heights of Dor; Solomon’s daughter Taphath was his wife;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-Abinadab, over all the district of Dor; Taphath, Solomon’s daughter, was his wife;

verses.rationale: Keeps the full geographic chain rather than shortening the roster.
verses.before: Baana son of Ahilud, over Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan, below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;
verses.after: Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and beyond Jokmeam;
verses.tsw_comparator: Baana son of Ahilud, over Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan, below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

verses.rationale: Retains both territories and the sixty fortified cities.
verses.before: Ben-Geber, in Ramoth-gilead; he had the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead; he had the region of Argob, which is in Bashan: sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars;
verses.after: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead, with the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead under him, and the region of Argob in Bashan—sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-Geber, in Ramoth-gilead; he had the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead; he had the region of Argob, which is in Bashan: sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars;

verses.rationale: Keeps the officer and place together.
verses.before: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
verses.after: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

verses.rationale: Preserves the second royal marriage connection.
verses.before: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he also took Basemath, Solomon’s daughter, as his wife;
verses.after: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he too had married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath;
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he also took Basemath, Solomon’s daughter, as his wife;

verses.rationale: Retains Bealoth as the pinned place form.
verses.before: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
verses.after: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
verses.tsw_comparator: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;

verses.rationale: Distinguishes this Jehoshaphat by his father.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
verses.after: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;

verses.rationale: Retains the patronymic without identifying him with the executed Shimei.
verses.before: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
verses.after: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
verses.tsw_comparator: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult closing administrative statement without silently inserting Judah.
verses.before: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead—the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan—and one governor who was in the land.
verses.after: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the territory of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan. There was one official in that land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead—the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan—and one governor who was in the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the abundance image and three ordinary activities.
verses.before: Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand that is by the sea. They were eating and drinking and rejoicing.
verses.after: Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand beside the sea. They ate, drank, and rejoiced.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand that is by the sea. They were eating and drinking and rejoicing.

verses.rationale: Retains the geographical range and tribute/service relationship.
verses.before: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt, bringing tribute and serving Solomon all the days of his life.
verses.after: Solomon ruled all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon throughout his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt, bringing tribute and serving Solomon all the days of his life.

verses.rationale: Keeps the large ancient measures rather than introducing uncertain conversions.
verses.before: Solomon’s provisions for one day were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of flour,
verses.after: Solomon’s daily provisions were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon’s provisions for one day were thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of flour,

verses.rationale: Retains all food categories and distinguishes the cattle’s feeding.
verses.before: ten fattened cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.
verses.after: ten fattened cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.
verses.tsw_comparator: ten fattened cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the geographical perspective while preserving repeated dominion.
verses.before: For he ruled over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River. And he had peace on every side around him.
verses.after: He ruled everything west of the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, including all the kings west of the River. He had peace on every side.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he ruled over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River. And he had peace on every side around him.

verses.rationale: Retains the concrete security image and traditional national extent.
verses.before: Judah and Israel lived in security, each under their vine and under their fig tree, from Dan to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.
verses.after: Throughout Solomon’s days, Judah and Israel lived securely, each under his own vine and fig tree, from Dan to Beer-sheba.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah and Israel lived in security, each under their vine and under their fig tree, from Dan to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.

verses.rationale: Keeps forty thousand from the pin without harmonizing Chronicles.
verses.before: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
verses.after: Solomon had forty thousand stalls for his chariot horses and twelve thousand horsemen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.

verses.rationale: Connects the roster with the table’s rotating support.
verses.before: These officials provided for King Solomon and for everyone who came near King Solomon’s table, each in their month; they let nothing be lacking.
verses.after: The district officials supplied King Solomon and everyone who came to his table, each in his assigned month. They let nothing be lacking.
verses.tsw_comparator: These officials provided for King Solomon and for all who came near King Solomon’s table, each in their month; they let nothing be lacking.

verses.rationale: Retains the second equine term without asserting a breed.
verses.before: They brought the barley and the straw for the horses and the steeds to the place where they were, each according to their assignment.
verses.after: Each also brought barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds to the required place, according to his assignment.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought the barley and the straw for the horses and the steeds to the place where they were, each according to their assignment.

verses.rationale: Preserves the heart image and its echoed sand comparison.
verses.before: God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.
verses.after: God gave Solomon wisdom, very great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.
verses.tsw_comparator: God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.

verses.rationale: Retains both comparative traditions.
verses.before: Solomon’s wisdom exceeded the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
verses.after: Solomon’s wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon’s wisdom exceeded the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps all named sages and the public reputation statement.
verses.before: He was wiser than every other person—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His name was known among all the nations around him.
verses.after: He was wiser than anyone: wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His name became known among all the surrounding nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was wiser than every other person—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His name was known among all the nations around him.

verses.rationale: Preserves both literary counts precisely.
verses.before: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered one thousand and five.
verses.after: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered one thousand five.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered one thousand and five.

verses.rationale: Keeps the botanical range and all four animal categories.
verses.before: He spoke about the trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He spoke also about animals, birds, creeping things, and fish.
verses.after: He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing out of a wall. He also spoke about animals, birds, crawling creatures, and fish.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke about the trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He spoke also about animals, birds, creeping things, and fish.

verses.rationale: Makes the emissary relationship readable without reducing the universal rhetoric.
verses.before: People came from all peoples to hear Solomon’s wisdom, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
verses.after: People came from all nations to hear Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: People came from all peoples to hear Solomon’s wisdom, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

verses.rationale: Retains the succession occasion and longstanding affection.
verses.before: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had loved David all his days.
verses.after: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon when he heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place. Hiram had always loved David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had loved David all his days.

verses.rationale: Introduces the ensuing direct message simply.
verses.before: Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying,
verses.after: Solomon sent this message to Hiram:
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying,

verses.rationale: Follows the read form my feet, noting the written his feet without silently harmonizing it.
verses.before: “You know that David my father was not able to build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the warfare that surrounded him, until the LORD put them under the soles of my feet.
verses.after: “You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the warfare surrounding him, until the LORD put his enemies under the soles of my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You know that David my father was not able to build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the warfare that surrounded him, until the LORD put them under the soles of my feet.

verses.rationale: Keeps adversary as a common noun and the twofold absence of trouble.
verses.before: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There is no adversary and no evil occurrence.
verses.after: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There is no adversary and no evil happening.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There is no adversary and no evil occurrence.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated house and Name language linking promise and construction.
verses.before: So I am planning to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will set in your place on your throne—he will build the house for my name.’
verses.after: So I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David: ‘Your son, whom I will put on your throne in your place, will build the house for my name.’
verses.tsw_comparator: So I am planning to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will set in your place on your throne—he will build the house for my name.’

verses.rationale: Preserves labor collaboration, pay and recognition of expertise.
verses.before: “Now command that they cut cedars from Lebanon for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will give you the wages of your servants according to all that you say. For you know that among us there is no one who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”
verses.after: Now give orders for cedars to be cut for me in Lebanon. My servants will work with yours, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set. You know that none of us knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now command that they cut cedars from Lebanon for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will give you the wages of your servants according to all that you say. For you know that among us there is no one who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Hiram’s praise and the reason for it.
verses.before: When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD today, who has given David a wise son over this great people.”
verses.after: When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he was delighted. “Blessed be the LORD today,” he said, “who has given David a wise son to rule this great people!”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD today, who has given David a wise son over this great people.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the two timber types without flattening them to lumber.
verses.before: Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, “I have heard what you sent to me. I will do all that you desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.
verses.after: Hiram sent word to Solomon: “I have heard your message. I will meet all your needs for cedar and cypress timber.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, “I have heard what you sent to me. I will do all that you desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.

verses.rationale: Unfolds transport and exchange into clear consecutive actions.
verses.before: My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts on the sea as far as the place you direct me. I will break them apart there, and you will carry them away. You, in turn, will do what I desire by providing food for my household.”
verses.after: My servants will bring it down from Lebanon to the sea. I will make it into rafts and float it to the place you designate. I will break the rafts apart there, and you can take the timber away. In return, meet my needs by supplying food for my household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts on the sea as far as the place you direct me. I will break them apart there, and you will carry them away. You, in turn, will do what I desire by providing food for my household.”

verses.rationale: Retains the fulfillment of the timber request.
verses.before: So Hiram supplied Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber, all that he desired.
verses.after: Hiram supplied Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Hiram supplied Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber, all that he desired.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unequal quantities, oil preparation and annual recurrence.
verses.before: Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year after year.
verses.after: Solomon supplied Hiram with twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household and twenty cors of beaten olive oil. He gave Hiram this amount year after year.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year after year.

verses.rationale: Retains wisdom, peace and covenant as connected but distinct claims.
verses.before: The LORD gave wisdom to Solomon, as he had spoken to him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.
verses.after: The LORD gave Solomon wisdom as he had promised. Hiram and Solomon were at peace, and the two made a covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gave wisdom to Solomon, as he had spoken to him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.

verses.rationale: Makes coercion explicit and preserves the Israelite levy.
verses.before: King Solomon conscripted forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor force numbered thirty thousand men.
verses.after: King Solomon conscripted a forced-labor levy from all Israel: thirty thousand men.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon conscripted forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor force numbered thirty thousand men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rotation and its overseer visible.
verses.before: He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month: they would be in Lebanon one month and at home two months. Adoniram was over the forced labor.
verses.after: He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month. They spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was over the forced labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month: they would be in Lebanon one month and at home two months. Adoniram was over the forced labor.

verses.rationale: Preserves the separate work groups and counts.
verses.before: Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
verses.after: Solomon also had seventy thousand burden bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hills,
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,

verses.rationale: Keeps this passage’s supervisor count without importing a parallel.
verses.before: besides Solomon’s chief officers over the work: three thousand three hundred who ruled over the people doing the work.
verses.after: besides Solomon’s thirty-three hundred chief overseers, who supervised the people doing the work.
verses.tsw_comparator: besides Solomon’s chief officers over the work: three thousand three hundred who ruled over the people doing the work.

verses.rationale: Retains the stones’ size, value and preparation.
verses.before: At the king’s command they quarried large stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.
verses.after: At the king’s command they quarried great, costly stones, dressed stones for the house’s foundations.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the king’s command they quarried large stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.

verses.rationale: Retains the three groups and both materials.
verses.before: Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, shaped the timber and the stones to build the house.
verses.after: Solomon’s builders, Hiram’s builders, and the Gebalites dressed the stone and prepared the timber and stone for building the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, shaped the timber and the stones to build the house.

verses.rationale: Preserves both chronological anchors and identifies the named month.
verses.before: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house for the LORD.
verses.after: In the four hundred eightieth year after the Israelites left Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in Ziv, the second month, he began building the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house for the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three dimensions and the ancient unit.
verses.before: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
verses.after: The house King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.

verses.rationale: Makes the porch’s orientation understandable without altering dimensions.
verses.before: The portico before the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, across the width of the house; it was ten cubits wide across the front of the house.
verses.after: The porch in front of the house’s main hall extended twenty cubits across the width of the house and projected ten cubits from its front.
verses.tsw_comparator: The portico before the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, across the width of the house; it was ten cubits wide across the front of the house.

verses.rationale: Uses a restrained architectural rendering; the uncertain expression is noted.
verses.before: He made windows for the house with recessed frames and lattices.
verses.after: He made windows for the house with recessed frames.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made windows for the house with recessed frames and lattices.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the surrounding structure from the two principal interior spaces.
verses.before: Against the wall of the house he built a structure all around, against the walls of the house surrounding the nave and the inner sanctuary; and he made side chambers all around.
verses.after: He built a structure against the outside walls of the house, around the main hall and the inner sanctuary, with side rooms all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: Against the wall of the house he built a structure all around, against the walls of the house surrounding the nave and the inner sanctuary; and he made side chambers all around.

verses.rationale: Explains the widths and wall ledges without inventing a building plan.
verses.before: The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle one six cubits wide, and the third seven cubits wide. For he made offsets around the outside of the house, so that the beams would not be fastened into the walls of the house.
verses.after: The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle one six, and the third seven. He made ledges around the outside of the house so the beams would not be inserted into its walls.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle one six cubits wide, and the third seven cubits wide. For he made offsets around the outside of the house, so that the beams would not be fastened into the walls of the house.

verses.rationale: Retains the silence motif and all named tools.
verses.before: When the house was built, it was built of finished stone prepared at the quarry; no hammer, axe, or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
verses.after: The house was built with stone finished at the quarry. No hammer, axe, or other iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the house was built, it was built of finished stone prepared at the quarry; no hammer, axe, or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned middle entrance despite the architectural difficulty.
verses.before: The entrance to the middle story was on the right side of the house. By winding stairs they went up to the middle story, and from the middle story to the third.
verses.after: The entrance to the middle side story was on the right side of the house. Winding stairs led up to the middle story and from there to the third.
verses.tsw_comparator: The entrance to the middle story was on the right side of the house. By winding stairs they went up to the middle story, and from the middle story to the third.

verses.rationale: Retains completion and distinguishes roof components.
verses.before: So he built the house and completed it. He roofed the house with beams and rows of cedar.
verses.after: He built the house and finished it, roofing it with cedar beams and boards.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he built the house and completed it. He roofed the house with beams and rows of cedar.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the height as story height in the surrounding structure.
verses.before: He built the side structure against the whole house, five cubits high, and fastened it to the house with cedar timbers.
verses.after: He built the side structure around the whole house, each story five cubits high, and attached it to the house with cedar timbers.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built the side structure against the whole house, five cubits high, and fastened it to the house with cedar timbers.

verses.rationale: Preserves the interruption of construction by divine speech.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Solomon:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon:

verses.rationale: Keeps the promise conditional on obedience rather than on construction alone.
verses.before: “Concerning this house that you are building: if you walk in my statutes, carry out my judgments, and keep all my commandments by walking in them, then I will establish with you my word that I spoke to David your father.
verses.after: “As for this house you are building: if you walk in my statutes, carry out my judgments, and keep all my commands by following them, I will fulfill with you the promise I made to your father David.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Concerning this house that you are building: if you walk in my statutes, carry out my judgments, and keep all my commandments by walking in them, then I will establish with you my word that I spoke to David your father.

verses.rationale: Retains dwelling among the people, not only within the building.
verses.before: I will dwell among the Israelites, and I will not forsake my people Israel.”
verses.after: I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will dwell among the Israelites, and I will not forsake my people Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated completion statement.
verses.before: So Solomon built the house and completed it.
verses.after: So Solomon built the house and finished it.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Solomon built the house and completed it.

verses.rationale: Makes the wood surfaces distinct while retaining both species.
verses.before: He built the inner walls of the house with cedar boards. From the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling, he overlaid the interior with wood; and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
verses.after: He lined the inside walls with cedar boards, covering them with wood from the floor to the ceiling, and laid cypress boards over the floor.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built the inner walls of the house with cedar boards. From the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling, he overlaid the interior with wood; and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult walls wording and the sanctuary’s two designations.
verses.before: He built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with cedar boards, from floor to walls, and built this within as an inner sanctuary, as the most holy place.
verses.after: He partitioned off twenty cubits at the rear of the house with cedar boards from the floor up to the walls. Inside, he made this the inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with cedar boards, from floor to walls, and built this within as an inner sanctuary, as the most holy place.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the relation of the hall to the rear sanctuary.
verses.before: The house—that is, the nave before it—was forty cubits long.
verses.after: The main hall in front of it was forty cubits long.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house—that is, the nave before it—was forty cubits long.

verses.rationale: Retains decoration and the emphatic concealment of stone.
verses.before: The cedar within the house was carved with gourds and open flowers. All was cedar; no stone was visible.
verses.after: The cedar inside the house was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; no stone could be seen.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cedar within the house was carved with gourds and open flowers. All was cedar; no stone was visible.

verses.rationale: Keeps purpose and inward location together.
verses.before: He prepared an inner sanctuary within the house, to place there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
verses.after: He prepared the inner sanctuary deep within the house to hold the ark of the LORD’s covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: He prepared an inner sanctuary within the house, to place there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the cube dimensions and the altar’s cedar covering.
verses.before: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid it with pure gold; he also overlaid the cedar altar.
verses.after: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty wide, and twenty high. He overlaid it with pure gold and covered the altar with cedar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid it with pure gold; he also overlaid the cedar altar.

verses.rationale: Retains chains and the repeated gold covering without defining their function.
verses.before: Solomon overlaid the interior of the house with pure gold. He drew chains of gold across the front of the inner sanctuary and overlaid it with gold.
verses.after: Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold. He stretched gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary and overlaid it with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon overlaid the interior of the house with pure gold. He drew chains of gold across the front of the inner sanctuary and overlaid it with gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated totality and the altar’s association.
verses.before: He overlaid the whole house with gold until the whole house was complete. He also overlaid with gold the whole altar belonging to the inner sanctuary.
verses.after: He covered the entire house with gold, until the whole house was finished. He also covered the entire altar belonging to the inner sanctuary with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: He overlaid the whole house with gold until the whole house was complete. He also overlaid with gold the whole altar belonging to the inner sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Retains the beings’ biblical name, wood and height.
