verses.before: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
verses.after: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.

verses.rationale: Makes the wingspan arithmetic audible.
verses.before: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits: ten cubits from the end of one wing to the end of the other.
verses.after: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other was five cubits: ten cubits from wingtip to wingtip.
verses.tsw_comparator: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits: ten cubits from the end of one wing to the end of the other.

verses.rationale: Retains equivalence rather than omitting the second measurement.
verses.before: The second cherub was ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measure and the same form.
verses.after: The second cherub also measured ten cubits. Both cherubim had the same dimensions and shape.
verses.tsw_comparator: The second cherub was ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measure and the same form.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated equal heights.
verses.before: The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was that of the second cherub.
verses.after: The first cherub was ten cubits high, and so was the second.
verses.tsw_comparator: The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was that of the second cherub.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the wing arrangement into a readable spatial description.
verses.before: He placed the cherubim within the inner house. The cherubim spread out their wings, so that the wing of one touched one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; their wings touched wing to wing in the middle of the house.
verses.after: He placed the cherubim inside the innermost room. Their wings were spread out: one cherub’s wing touched one wall, the other’s wing touched the opposite wall, and their wings met in the middle of the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed the cherubim within the inner house. The cherubim spread out their wings, so that the wing of one touched one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; their wings touched wing to wing in the middle of the house.

verses.rationale: Retains their covering in a short sentence.
verses.before: He overlaid the cherubim with gold.
verses.after: He overlaid the cherubim with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: He overlaid the cherubim with gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three motifs and both rooms.
verses.before: On all the walls of the house, inside and outside, he carved engraved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
verses.after: All around the house’s walls, in both the inner and outer rooms, he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
verses.tsw_comparator: On all the walls of the house, inside and outside, he carved engraved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.

verses.rationale: Retains gold flooring throughout the two spaces.
verses.before: He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
verses.after: He covered the floor with gold in both the inner and outer rooms.
verses.tsw_comparator: He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.

verses.rationale: Uses the five-sided interpretation while marking its uncertainty in a note.
verses.before: For the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the doorposts were five-sided.
verses.after: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made olive-wood doors, with a five-sided doorframe.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the doorposts were five-sided.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ornament list and gold application distinct.
verses.before: The two doors were of olive wood. He carved on them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold. He spread the gold over the cherubim and the palm trees.
verses.after: On the two olive-wood doors he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers. He overlaid the doors with gold, spreading it over the cherubim and palm trees.
verses.tsw_comparator: The two doors were of olive wood. He carved on them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold. He spread the gold over the cherubim and the palm trees.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast with the preceding frame interpretation.
verses.before: So also, for the entrance of the nave, he made doorposts of olive wood, four-sided.
verses.after: For the entrance to the main hall he likewise made olive-wood doorposts, with a four-sided frame,
verses.tsw_comparator: So also, for the entrance of the nave, he made doorposts of olive wood, four-sided.

verses.rationale: Makes the paired folding construction clear.
verses.before: The two doors were of cypress wood. The two leaves of one door folded, and the two leaves of the other door folded.
verses.after: and two cypress doors. Each door had two folding panels.
verses.tsw_comparator: The two doors were of cypress wood. The two leaves of one door folded, and the two leaves of the other door folded.

verses.rationale: Retains the relief-shaped gold covering.
verses.before: He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, fitted evenly over the carved work.
verses.after: He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them and covered them with gold fitted to the carvings.
verses.tsw_comparator: He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, fitted evenly over the carved work.

verses.rationale: Keeps the masonry/timber ratio and court distinction.
verses.before: He built the inner court with three rows of cut stone and one row of cedar beams.
verses.after: He built the inner court with three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built the inner court with three rows of cut stone and one row of cedar beams.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated foundation date.
verses.before: In the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.
verses.after: The foundation of the LORD’s house was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.

verses.rationale: Retains both dates, completion scope and stated duration.
verses.before: In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was completed in all its details and according to all its specifications. He built it in seven years.
verses.after: In the eleventh year, in Bul, the eighth month, the house was finished in all its details and according to all its specifications. He spent seven years building it.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was completed in all its details and according to all its specifications. He built it in seven years.

verses.rationale: Preserves the duration beside the temple’s seven years.
verses.before: Solomon took thirteen years to build his own house, and he completed all his house.
verses.after: Solomon spent thirteen years building his own house, completing the whole complex.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon took thirteen years to build his own house, and he completed all his house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the building name, dimensions and four rows.
verses.before: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon: its length was one hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits. It stood on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.
verses.after: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, a hundred cubits long, fifty wide, and thirty high, on four rows of cedar pillars with cedar beams on the pillars.
verses.tsw_comparator: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon: its length was one hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits. It stood on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.

verses.rationale: Makes the counted elements explicit while noting the architectural uncertainty.
verses.before: It was roofed with cedar above the side chambers that were upon the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen in each row.
verses.after: It was roofed with cedar above the beams resting on the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen to a row.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was roofed with cedar above the side chambers that were upon the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen in each row.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated threefold arrangement.
verses.before: There were three rows of windows, with window facing window three times over.
verses.after: There were three rows of windows, facing one another in three tiers.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were three rows of windows, with window facing window three times over.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes doorframes from opposing openings.
verses.before: All the doorways and doorposts were square in shape, and window faced window three times over.
verses.after: All the doorways and their frames were rectangular, and the windows faced one another in three tiers.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the doorways and doorposts were square in shape, and window faced window three times over.

verses.rationale: Retains the hall, porch and uncertain canopy term without embellishing.
verses.before: He made the Hall of Pillars: its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits. A porch was before them, with pillars and a canopy before them.
verses.after: He made the Hall of Pillars fifty cubits long and thirty wide. A porch stood in front of it, with pillars and a canopy before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the Hall of Pillars: its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits. A porch was before them, with pillars and a canopy before them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the hall’s paired names and the pinned floor-to-floor expression.
verses.before: He made the Hall of the Throne, where he would give judgment—the Hall of Judgment. It was paneled with cedar from floor to floor.
verses.after: He made the Hall of the Throne, where he would give judgment—the Hall of Justice. It was paneled with cedar from one end of the floor to the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the Hall of the Throne, where he would give judgment—the Hall of Judgment. It was paneled with cedar from floor to floor.

verses.rationale: Preserves the separate residence and wife’s house.
verses.before: His house, where he was to live, was in the other court, behind the hall, and was of the same construction. Solomon also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had taken.
verses.after: His own residence, in another court behind the hall, was built in the same way. He also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.
verses.tsw_comparator: His house, where he was to live, was in the other court, behind the hall, and was of the same construction. Solomon also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had taken.

verses.rationale: Keeps material preparation and the full architectural extent.
verses.before: All these were of costly stones, cut to measure, sawed with saws inside and out, from foundation to coping, and from outside to the great court.
verses.after: All these buildings used costly stones, cut to size and sawn on their inner and outer faces, from the foundations to the coping and outside as far as the great court.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these were of costly stones, cut to measure, sawed with saws inside and out, from foundation to coping, and from outside to the great court.

verses.rationale: Preserves both sizes without converting units.
verses.before: The foundations were of costly, large stones—stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
verses.after: The foundations were of great, costly stones, some ten cubits and some eight cubits long.
verses.tsw_comparator: The foundations were of costly, large stones—stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.

verses.rationale: Keeps the upper materials distinct from foundations.
verses.before: Above were costly stones, cut to measure, and cedar.
verses.after: Above them were costly stones cut to size, and cedar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Above were costly stones, cut to measure, and cedar.

verses.rationale: Retains the shared construction pattern and all three spaces.
verses.before: The great court surrounding them had three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams, as did the inner court of the house of the LORD and the porch of the house.
verses.after: The great court was surrounded by three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams, as were the inner court of the LORD’s house and the house’s porch.
verses.tsw_comparator: The great court surrounding them had three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams, as did the inner court of the house of the LORD and the porch of the house.

verses.rationale: Introduces the craftsman without conflating him with the king of Tyre.
verses.before: King Solomon sent for Hiram and brought him from Tyre.
verses.after: King Solomon sent for Hiram from Tyre.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon sent for Hiram and brought him from Tyre.

verses.rationale: Preserves the parentage from this pin and the threefold craft qualification.
verses.before: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
verses.after: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali; his father was a Tyrian bronze worker. Hiram was filled with wisdom, understanding, and skill for every kind of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and did all his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s distribution of measurements between the pillars.
verses.before: He cast the two bronze pillars. Each pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a cord of twelve cubits measured around each pillar.
verses.after: He cast the two bronze pillars. One pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a cord twelve cubits long went around the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: He cast the two bronze pillars. Each pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a cord of twelve cubits measured around each pillar.

verses.rationale: Preserves material, position and equal heights.
verses.before: He made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars. The height of one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits.
verses.after: He made two cast-bronze capitals to set on top of the pillars. Each capital was five cubits high.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars. The height of one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two sets of seven in the difficult ornament description.
verses.before: There were latticeworks, netted work, and chains, braided work, for the capitals on the tops of the pillars: seven for one capital and seven for the other capital.
verses.after: For the capitals on top of the pillars he made latticework, with twisted chains: seven for one capital and seven for the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were latticeworks, netted work, and chains, braided work, for the capitals on the tops of the pillars: seven for one capital and seven for the other capital.

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned pillars/pomegranates order; textual difficulty is noted rather than silently transposed.
verses.before: He made the pillars, with two rows all around on the one latticework to cover the capitals that were above the pomegranates; and he did the same for the other capital.
verses.after: He made the pillars and two rows around one lattice to cover the capitals above the pomegranates. He did the same for the other capital.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the pillars, with two rows all around on the one latticework to cover the capitals that were above the pomegranates; and he did the same for the other capital.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four-cubit floral element beside the five-cubit total.
verses.before: The capitals that were on the tops of the pillars in the porch were lily work, four cubits high.
verses.after: The capitals on top of the pillars in the porch had lily-shaped work, four cubits high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The capitals that were on the tops of the pillars in the porch were lily work, four cubits high.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s other-capital phrasing and ornament count.
verses.before: The capitals on the two pillars also had two hundred pomegranates in rows all around, above and opposite the rounded projection beside the latticework, on the other capital.
verses.after: On both pillars the capitals rose above the bowl-shaped part beside the lattice. Two hundred pomegranates ran in rows around the other capital.
verses.tsw_comparator: The capitals on the two pillars also had two hundred pomegranates in rows all around, above and opposite the rounded projection beside the latticework, on the other capital.

verses.rationale: Preserves side and name relationships.
verses.before: He set up the pillars at the porch of the temple. He set up the right-hand pillar and named it Jachin. He set up the left-hand pillar and named it Boaz.
verses.after: He set up the pillars at the main hall’s porch. He named the right pillar Jachin and the left pillar Boaz.
verses.tsw_comparator: He set up the pillars at the porch of the temple. He set up the right-hand pillar and named it Jachin. He set up the left-hand pillar and named it Boaz.

verses.rationale: Retains floral completion as a separate statement.
verses.before: Lily work was on the tops of the pillars. So the work of the pillars was finished.
verses.after: The tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work on the pillars was finished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lily work was on the tops of the pillars. So the work of the pillars was finished.

verses.rationale: Keeps the Sea name and all measurements without mathematical correction.
verses.before: He made the Sea, cast in metal, ten cubits from rim to rim, circular all around. It was five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured around it.
verses.after: He made the cast-metal Sea, circular in shape, ten cubits from rim to rim and five cubits high. A cord thirty cubits long went around it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the Sea, cast in metal, ten cubits from rim to rim, circular all around. It was five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured around it.

verses.rationale: Retains count, rows and integrated casting.
verses.before: Below its rim, gourds encircled it all around, ten to a cubit. The gourds were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.
verses.after: Under its rim, gourds encircled it, ten to a cubit. The gourds were in two rows, cast as one piece with the Sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Below its rim, gourds encircled it all around, ten to a cubit. The gourds were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four directional groups and orientation.
verses.before: It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea was above them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.
verses.after: It stood on twelve cattle: three facing north, three west, three south, and three east. The Sea rested on them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.
verses.tsw_comparator: It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea was above them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.

verses.rationale: Keeps thickness, floral simile and the pinned capacity.
verses.before: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held two thousand baths.
verses.after: It was a handbreadth thick. Its rim was shaped like a cup’s rim, like a lily blossom. It held two thousand baths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held two thousand baths.

verses.rationale: Preserves the number and three dimensions of the stands.
verses.before: He made ten bronze stands. Each stand was four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
verses.after: He made ten bronze stands, each four cubits long, four wide, and three high.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made ten bronze stands. Each stand was four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.

verses.rationale: Introduces construction details with restrained technical language.
verses.before: This was the construction of the stands: they had panels, and the panels were set between frames.
verses.after: This was how the stands were made: they had panels fitted between crossbars.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was the construction of the stands: they had panels, and the panels were set between frames.

verses.rationale: Retains the three figures and difficult ledge/wreath arrangement.
verses.before: On the panels between the frames were lions, oxen, and cherubim. Above the frames was a pedestal, and beneath the lions and oxen were descending wreaths.
verses.after: On the panels between the crossbars were lions, cattle, and cherubim. Above, on the crossbars, was a supporting ledge, and below the lions and cattle were hanging wreaths.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the panels between the frames were lions, oxen, and cherubim. Above the frames was a pedestal, and beneath the lions and oxen were descending wreaths.

verses.rationale: Keeps wheels, axles, corner supports and decoration distinct.
verses.before: Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles. Its four feet had supports; beneath the basin the supports were cast, with wreaths beside each person.
verses.after: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles. Its four corners had cast supports under the basin, with wreaths beside each support.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles. Its four feet had supports; beneath the basin the supports were cast, with wreaths beside each one.

verses.rationale: Preserves upward extension, contrasting shapes and dimensions; compressed referents remain uncertain and are noted.
verses.before: Its opening was within a crown that rose one cubit above it. Its opening was round, like the work of a stand, a cubit and a half wide. There were carvings also on its opening, but its panels were square, not round.
verses.after: From inside the crown, its opening rose a cubit above it. The opening was round, shaped like a pedestal, a cubit and a half across. It too had carvings. The panels, however, were square, not round.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its opening was within a crown that rose one cubit above it. Its opening was round, like the work of a stand, a cubit and a half wide. There were carvings also on its opening, but its panels were square, not round.

verses.rationale: Keeps wheel position, attachment and size.
verses.before: The four wheels were beneath the panels, and the wheel-axles were attached to the stand. The height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
verses.after: The four wheels were below the panels, with their axles attached to the stand. Each wheel was a cubit and a half high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The four wheels were beneath the panels, and the wheel-axles were attached to the stand. The height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.

verses.rationale: Retains the chariot comparison and four parts.
verses.before: The construction of the wheels was like the construction of chariot wheels: their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all cast.
verses.after: The wheels were made like chariot wheels. Their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all cast metal.
verses.tsw_comparator: The construction of the wheels was like the construction of chariot wheels: their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all cast.

verses.rationale: Keeps the integral construction explicit.
verses.before: There were four supports at the four corners of each stand; the supports were part of the stand itself.
verses.after: Each stand had four supports at its four corners, made as one piece with the stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were four supports at the four corners of each stand; the supports were part of the stand itself.

verses.rationale: Preserves the upper band’s shape, height and joined components.
verses.before: At the top of the stand was a circular band, half a cubit high. The handles and panels at the top of the stand were part of it.
verses.after: At the top of each stand was a round band half a cubit high. Its supports and panels were made as one piece with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the top of the stand was a circular band, half a cubit high. The handles and panels at the top of the stand were part of it.

verses.rationale: Keeps decoration adapted to the available surface.
verses.before: He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the panels of its handles and on its panels, wherever there was space for each, with wreaths all around.
verses.after: On the surfaces of its supports and panels he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees wherever there was room, with wreaths all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the panels of its handles and on its panels, wherever there was space for each, with wreaths all around.

verses.rationale: Retains the threefold identity statement.
verses.before: In this way he made the ten stands. All were cast alike, of one measure and one form.
verses.after: He made all ten stands alike: the same casting, dimensions, and shape.
verses.tsw_comparator: In this way he made the ten stands. All were cast alike, of one measure and one form.

verses.rationale: Preserves capacity and measurement without inventing an unstated dimension.
verses.before: He made ten bronze basins. Each basin held forty baths and was four cubits across. There was one basin on each of the ten stands.
verses.after: He made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths and measuring four cubits. There was one basin on each of the ten stands.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made ten bronze basins. Each basin held forty baths and was four cubits across. There was one basin on each of the ten stands.

verses.rationale: Makes the five/five arrangement and Sea location readable.
verses.before: He placed five stands on the right side of the house and five on the left side of the house. He placed the Sea on the right side of the house, toward the east, opposite the south.
verses.after: He placed five stands on the right side of the house and five on the left. He put the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed five stands on the right side of the house and five on the left side of the house. He placed the Sea on the right side of the house, toward the east, opposite the south.

verses.rationale: Keeps basins in this verse rather than harmonizing the later pots list.
verses.before: Hiram made the basins, the shovels, and the bowls. So Hiram completed all the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:
verses.after: Hiram made the basins, shovels, and bowls. He finished all the work he did for King Solomon on the LORD’s house:
verses.tsw_comparator: Hiram made the basins, the shovels, and the bowls. So Hiram completed all the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:

verses.rationale: Retains the inventory’s paired items.
verses.before: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars; the two latticeworks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars;
verses.after: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of them; the two lattices covering those capitals;
verses.tsw_comparator: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars; the two latticeworks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on the tops of the pillars;

verses.rationale: Preserves total, distribution and location.
verses.before: the four hundred pomegranates for the two latticeworks—two rows of pomegranates for each latticework, covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on the fronts of the pillars;
verses.after: the four hundred pomegranates for the two lattices, two rows for each lattice, covering the two bowl-shaped capitals at the tops of the pillars;
verses.tsw_comparator: the four hundred pomegranates for the two latticeworks—two rows of pomegranates for each latticework, covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on the fronts of the pillars;

verses.rationale: Keeps both counts in the repeated inventory.
verses.before: the ten stands and the ten basins upon the stands;
verses.after: the ten stands and the ten basins on them;
verses.tsw_comparator: the ten stands and the ten basins upon the stands;

verses.rationale: Retains the singular vessel and twelve supports.
verses.before: the one Sea and the twelve oxen beneath the Sea;
verses.after: the one Sea and the twelve cattle underneath it;
verses.tsw_comparator: the one Sea and the twelve oxen beneath the Sea;

verses.rationale: Follows the read these form and retains polished material.
verses.before: the pots, shovels, bowls, and all these vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, of burnished bronze.
verses.after: and the pots, shovels, and bowls. All these utensils that Hiram made for King Solomon for the LORD’s house were of polished bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: the pots, shovels, bowls, and all these vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, of burnished bronze.

verses.rationale: Keeps production method and both geographic limits.
verses.before: The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in clay molds between Succoth and Zarethan.
verses.after: The king had them cast in the clay ground of the Jordan plain between Succoth and Zarethan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in clay molds between Succoth and Zarethan.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic quantity and unspecified total.
verses.before: Solomon left all the vessels unweighed because they were exceedingly many; the weight of the bronze was not determined.
verses.after: Solomon left all the utensils unweighed because there were so many. The weight of the bronze was not determined.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon left all the vessels unweighed because they were exceedingly many; the weight of the bronze was not determined.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sacred bread designation and gold items.
verses.before: Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of the LORD: the gold altar; the gold table on which was the bread of the Presence;
verses.after: Solomon made all the furnishings for the LORD’s house: the gold altar; the gold table for the bread of the Presence;
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of the LORD: the gold altar; the gold table on which was the bread of the Presence;

verses.rationale: Preserves the five/five arrangement and accessory list.
verses.before: the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left before the inner sanctuary; the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold;
verses.after: the pure-gold lampstands, five on the right and five on the left before the inner sanctuary; the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;
verses.tsw_comparator: the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left before the inner sanctuary; the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold;

verses.rationale: Retains all utensils and both sets of door fittings.
verses.before: the basins, wick trimmers, bowls, ladles, and firepans of pure gold; and the sockets for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, the temple—of gold.
verses.after: the cups, snuffers, bowls, dishes, and firepans of pure gold; and the gold sockets for the doors of the innermost room, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the main hall.
verses.tsw_comparator: the basins, wick trimmers, bowls, ladles, and firepans of pure gold; and the sockets for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, the temple—of gold.

verses.rationale: Keeps completion and inherited dedicated property distinct.
verses.before: Thus all the work that King Solomon did for the house of the LORD was completed. Solomon brought in the holy gifts of David his father—the silver, the gold, and the vessels—and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
verses.after: When all King Solomon’s work on the LORD’s house was finished, he brought in the things his father David had dedicated. He placed the silver, gold, and utensils in the treasuries of the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus all the work that King Solomon did for the house of the LORD was completed. Solomon brought in the holy gifts of David his father—the silver, the gold, and the vessels—and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves leadership groups and identifies Zion without erasing the formal royal repetition.
verses.before: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel—all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the people of Israel—before King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.
verses.after: Then Solomon assembled Israel’s elders, all the tribal heads and leaders of the ancestral families of the Israelites, before King Solomon in Jerusalem. They were to bring up the ark of the LORD’s covenant from the City of David, which is Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel—all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the people of Israel—before King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.

verses.rationale: Keeps the gendered assembly and both month designations.
verses.before: All the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon at the festival in the month Ethanim, the seventh month.
verses.after: All the men of Israel gathered before King Solomon at the festival in Ethanim, the seventh month.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon at the festival in the month Ethanim, the seventh month.

verses.rationale: Retains elders’ arrival before the priests’ action.
verses.before: When all the elders of Israel had come, the priests lifted the ark.
verses.after: When all Israel’s elders had arrived, the priests lifted the ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the elders of Israel had come, the priests lifted the ark.

verses.rationale: Keeps all transported objects and both groups.
verses.before: They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.
verses.after: They brought up the LORD’s ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils in the tent. The priests and Levites brought them up.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated counting language and abundance.
verses.before: King Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel gathered with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle too numerous to be counted or numbered.
verses.after: King Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel gathered with him stood before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted or numbered.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel gathered with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle too numerous to be counted or numbered.

verses.rationale: Keeps the nested sacred locations understandable.
verses.before: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD into its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the most holy place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.after: The priests brought the ark of the LORD’s covenant to its place in the house’s inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place, beneath the cherubim’s wings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD into its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the most holy place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.

verses.rationale: Retains the covering action and poles.
verses.before: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.
verses.after: The cherubim spread their wings over the ark’s place, sheltering the ark and its poles from above.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.

verses.rationale: Preserves visibility limits and the narrator’s temporal viewpoint.
verses.before: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen outside; and they are there to this day.
verses.after: The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside. They are there to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The poles were so long that the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen outside; and they are there to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exclusive contents statement without harmonizing other passages.
verses.before: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel when they came out from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Nothing was in the ark except the two stone tablets Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they left Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel when they came out from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains the sequence of departure and cloud.
verses.before: When the priests came out from the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD.
verses.after: When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the priests came out from the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps inability to minister and repeated divine Name.
verses.before: The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the LORD’s glory filled the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the darkness image in the opening declaration.
verses.before: Then Solomon said, “The LORD said that he would dwell in deep darkness.
verses.after: Then Solomon said, “The LORD said he would dwell in thick darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon said, “The LORD said that he would dwell in deep darkness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic claim and poetic parallel.
verses.before: I have indeed built you an exalted house, a settled place for you to dwell forever.”
verses.after: I have indeed built you a lofty house, a settled place for you to dwell forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I have indeed built you an exalted house, a settled place for you to dwell forever.”

verses.rationale: Makes the change of audience explicit.
verses.before: Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
verses.after: The king turned and blessed the whole assembly of Israel while they stood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.

verses.rationale: Retains the mouth/hand correspondence.
verses.before: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and has fulfilled it by his hand, saying,
verses.after: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, Israel’s God! With his own mouth he spoke to my father David, and with his own hand he fulfilled it. He said:

verses.rationale: Retains this claim beside the earlier Israelite levy without harmonization.

verses.rationale: Keeps the festival frequency and difficult completion clause.

verses.tsw_comparator: They were from the nations of which the LORD had said to the Israelites, “You must not enter among them, and they must not enter among you; surely they will turn your heart after their gods.” Solomon clung to them in love.

verses.rationale: Preserves status distinctions and both counts.
verses.before: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart away.
verses.after: He had seven hundred royal wives and three hundred concubines. His wives turned his heart away.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart away.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated heart and the narrator’s comparison.
verses.before: For when Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart after other gods; and his heart was not whole with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
verses.after: As Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods. His heart was not wholly with the LORD his God, as his father David’s heart had been.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart after other gods; and his heart was not whole with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.

verses.rationale: Retains named deities and evaluative language.
verses.before: Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the god of the Sidonians, and after Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites.
verses.after: Solomon followed Ashtoreth, goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the god of the Sidonians, and after Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit assessment of Solomon himself.
verses.before: Solomon did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and did not follow the LORD fully, as David his father had done.
verses.after: He did evil in the LORD’s eyes and did not follow the LORD fully, as his father David had.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and did not follow the LORD fully, as David his father had done.

verses.rationale: Keeps Molech rather than harmonizing Milcom; facing Jerusalem expresses the source relation without supplying a compass direction.
verses.before: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, on the mountain opposite Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the Ammonites.
verses.after: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable god of Moab, on the hill facing Jerusalem, and for Molech, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, on the mountain opposite Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the Ammonites.

verses.rationale: Preserves women as the worshiping subjects.
verses.before: So he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
verses.after: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned offerings and sacrificed to their gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.

verses.rationale: Keeps the twice-received revelation in the accusation.
verses.before: The LORD was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
verses.after: The LORD became angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the LORD, Israel’s God, who had appeared to him twice.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.

verses.rationale: Retains the specific prohibition and royal failure.
verses.before: He had commanded him concerning this matter, that he should not go after other gods; but he did not keep what the LORD had commanded.
verses.after: The LORD had commanded him about this very thing: he must not follow other gods. But Solomon did not keep the LORD’s command.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had commanded him concerning this matter, that he should not go after other gods; but he did not keep what the LORD had commanded.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic tearing and covenant breach.
verses.before: So the LORD said to Solomon, “Because this has been with you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
verses.after: So the LORD said to Solomon, “Since this is how you have acted, and you have not kept my covenant and the statutes I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD said to Solomon, “Because this has been with you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.

verses.rationale: Preserves delayed judgment and the hand image.
verses.before: Yet I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father. I will tear it from the hand of your son.
verses.after: But for your father David’s sake, I will not do it during your lifetime. I will tear it from your son’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father. I will tear it from the hand of your son.

verses.rationale: Retains one tribe without arithmetic harmonization.
verses.before: Yet I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”
verses.after: Still, I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give your son one tribe for the sake of my servant David and Jerusalem, which I chose.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”

verses.rationale: Keeps adversary as a human opponent raised by God.
verses.before: Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite. He was of the royal line in Edom.
verses.after: The LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, of the royal line in Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite. He was of the royal line in Edom.

verses.rationale: Preserves the all-male slaughter and burial context.
verses.before: For when David was in Edom, and Joab, commander of the army, went up to bury the slain, he struck down every male in Edom.
verses.after: When David was in Edom, Joab the army commander went up to bury the slain and struck down every male in Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when David was in Edom, and Joab, commander of the army, went up to bury the slain, he struck down every male in Edom.

verses.rationale: Retains duration and repeated totalizing claim.
verses.before: For Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
verses.after: Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom.

verses.rationale: Keeps the child survivor and his companions.
verses.before: Yet Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites from among his father’s servants with him, to go to Egypt. Hadad was a young boy.
verses.after: Hadad escaped to Egypt with some Edomite servants of his father. He was only a young boy.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites from among his father’s servants with him, to go to Egypt. Hadad was a young boy.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the refugee journey and three provisions.
verses.before: They set out from Midian and came to Paran. From Paran they took men with them and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave him a house, assigned him food, and gave him land.
verses.after: They left Midian and came to Paran. Taking men from Paran with them, they went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, assigned him food, and gave him land.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Midian and came to Paran. From Paran they took men with them and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave him a house, assigned him food, and gave him land.

verses.rationale: Makes the marriage relationship clear.
verses.before: Hadad found great favor in Pharaoh’s eyes, so that Pharaoh gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen mother.
verses.after: Hadad found great favor with Pharaoh, who gave him his wife’s sister in marriage—the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hadad found great favor in Pharaoh’s eyes, so that Pharaoh gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen mother.

verses.rationale: Keeps the aunt’s role and royal upbringing.
verses.before: The sister of Tahpenes bore him his son Genubath. Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh’s house, and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s house among Pharaoh’s children.
verses.after: Tahpenes’ sister bore him a son, Genubath. Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh’s house, and he lived there among Pharaoh’s sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sister of Tahpenes bore him his son Genubath. Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh’s house, and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s house among Pharaoh’s children.

verses.rationale: Preserves both deaths motivating the request.
verses.before: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David lay with his ancestors and that Joab, commander of the army, was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Send me away, so that I may go to my land.”
verses.after: While in Egypt, Hadad heard that David had lain down with his ancestors and that Joab the army commander was dead. He told Pharaoh, “Let me go back to my own land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David lay with his ancestors and that Joab, commander of the army, was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Send me away, so that I may go to my land.”

verses.rationale: Retains the unanswered motivation and emphatic request.
verses.before: Yet Pharaoh said to him, “What have you lacked while you were with me, that now you seek to go to your own land?” He said, “Nothing. But please, send me away.”
verses.after: Pharaoh asked him, “What do you lack here with me that makes you want to go to your own land?” “Nothing,” he answered. “But please, let me go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Pharaoh said to him, “What have you lacked while you were with me, that now you seek to go to your own land?” He said, “Nothing. But please, send me away.”

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct names and the fugitive’s former allegiance.
verses.before: God raised up another adversary against him: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
verses.after: God raised up another adversary against Solomon: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
verses.tsw_comparator: God raised up another adversary against him: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the slaughter’s referent while preserving the plural seizure of rule.
verses.before: He gathered men around himself and became leader of a band when David killed them. They went to Damascus, settled there, and became kings in Damascus.
verses.after: He gathered men around him and led a raiding band when David slaughtered Hadadezer’s forces. They went to Damascus, settled there, and took power in Damascus.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gathered men around himself and became leader of a band when David killed them. They went to Damascus, settled there, and became kings in Damascus.

verses.rationale: Makes the difficult added-harm clause readable without relocating rule to Edom.
verses.before: He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, along with the trouble that Hadad caused. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
verses.after: He was Israel’s adversary throughout Solomon’s days, adding to the harm Hadad did. He loathed Israel and ruled over Aram.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, along with the trouble that Hadad caused. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.

verses.rationale: Retains revolt image, origin and maternal identity.
verses.before: Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow, was Solomon’s servant; and he raised his hand against the king.
verses.after: Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, also raised his hand against the king. He was Solomon’s servant; his mother was a widow named Zeruah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow, was Solomon’s servant; and he raised his hand against the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps the construction context of the revolt.
verses.before: This was the reason he raised his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo and closed the breach in the city of David his father.
verses.after: This is how he came to raise his hand against the king. Solomon was building the Millo and closing the breach in the City of David his father.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was the reason he raised his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo and closed the breach in the city of David his father.

verses.rationale: Preserves ability and the particular labor jurisdiction.
verses.before: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of strength. Solomon saw that the young man was diligent in his work, and he put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
verses.after: Jeroboam was a capable man. When Solomon saw how industrious the young man was, he put him over all the forced labor of Joseph’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of strength. Solomon saw that the young man was diligent in his work, and he put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.

verses.rationale: Names the likely cloak wearer; ambiguity is noted.
verses.before: At that time, when Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Ahijah was wrapped in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the field.
verses.after: At that time, as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two were alone in the open country.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time, when Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Ahijah was wrapped in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new garment and symbolic number.
verses.before: Ahijah took hold of the new cloak that was on him and tore it into twelve pieces.
verses.after: Ahijah seized the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahijah took hold of the new cloak that was on him and tore it into twelve pieces.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ten-piece/ten-tribe interpretation.
verses.before: Then he said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Look, I am tearing the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and giving you ten tribes.
verses.after: He told Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces. For this is what the LORD, Israel’s God, says: ‘I am tearing the kingdom from Solomon’s hand and giving you ten tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Look, I am tearing the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and giving you ten tribes.

verses.rationale: Retains one despite twelve pieces and ten allotted.
verses.before: But one tribe will remain for him, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel.
verses.after: But one tribe will remain his, for the sake of my servant David and Jerusalem, the city I chose from all Israel’s tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: But one tribe will remain for him, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the plural they and singular his father shift.
verses.before: This is because they have forsaken me and bowed down to Ashtoreth, the god of the Sidonians; to Chemosh, the god of Moab; and to Milcom, the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my eyes, and keeping my statutes and my judgments, as David his father did.
verses.after: This is because they abandoned me and bowed to Ashtoreth, goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh, god of Moab, and Milcom, god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my eyes and keeping my statutes and judgments, as his father David did.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is because they have forsaken me and bowed down to Ashtoreth, the god of the Sidonians; to Chemosh, the god of Moab; and to Milcom, the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my eyes, and keeping my statutes and my judgments, as David his father did.

verses.rationale: Keeps lifetime restraint and the stated reason.
verses.before: Yet I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes.
verses.after: Yet I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand. I will keep him as ruler all his life for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose and who kept my commands and statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes.

verses.rationale: Retains the delayed transfer and number.
verses.before: Yet I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give it to you—ten tribes.
verses.after: I will take the kingship from his son’s hand and give you ten tribes.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give it to you—ten tribes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the lamp image and Name language.
verses.before: To his son I will give one tribe, so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city that I chose for myself, to put my name there.
verses.after: I will give his son one tribe, so my servant David may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city I chose for myself to place my name there.
verses.tsw_comparator: To his son I will give one tribe, so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city that I chose for myself, to put my name there.

verses.rationale: Keeps the breadth of the royal grant.
verses.before: I will take you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires, and you will be king over Israel.
verses.after: I will take you, and you will rule over all you desire. You will be king over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will take you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires, and you will be king over Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains Jeroboam’s conditional house promise parallel to David’s.
verses.before: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in my ways, and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, then I will be with you. I will build for you a faithful house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
verses.after: If you listen to all I command, walk in my ways, and do what is right in my eyes, keeping my statutes and commands as my servant David did, I will be with you. I will build you an enduring house, as I built for David, and give Israel to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in my ways, and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, then I will be with you. I will build for you a faithful house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the limit on affliction without specifying fulfillment.
verses.before: I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.”
verses.after: For this I will afflict David’s descendants, but not forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.”

verses.rationale: Preserves royal violence and the named protector.
verses.before: Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death. But Jeroboam rose up and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he remained in Egypt until Solomon’s death.
verses.after: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt and stayed in Egypt until Solomon died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death. But Jeroboam rose up and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he remained in Egypt until Solomon’s death.

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s source citation as a question.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did, and his wisdom—are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
verses.after: The rest of Solomon’s history, all he did, and his wisdom—are they not written in the Book of Solomon’s Acts?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did, and his wisdom—are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?

verses.rationale: Keeps scope, capital and duration.
verses.before: The time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
verses.after: Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem for forty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.

verses.rationale: Retains death idiom, burial and succession.
verses.before: Then Solomon lay with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David his father. Rehoboam his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Solomon lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David his father. His son Rehoboam became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon lay with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David his father. Rehoboam his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keeps assembly location and purpose.
verses.before: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
verses.after: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.

verses.rationale: Preserves remained in Egypt rather than importing returned.
verses.before: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it—he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon, and Jeroboam remained in Egypt—
verses.after: Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it while he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon. Jeroboam was living in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it—he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon, and Jeroboam remained in Egypt—

verses.rationale: Makes the summons and joint address sequential.
verses.before: they sent and called for him. Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.after: They sent for him. Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
verses.tsw_comparator: they sent and called for him. Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains yoke and repeated service language.
verses.before: “Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he placed upon us, and we will serve you.”
verses.after: “Your father made our yoke harsh. Now lighten the harsh service and heavy yoke your father put on us, and we will serve you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he placed upon us, and we will serve you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the delay and response.
verses.before: He said to them, “Go away for three days, then return to me.” So the people went away.
verses.after: He told them, “Go away for three days, then return to me.” So the people left.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “Go away for three days, then return to me.” So the people went away.

verses.rationale: Identifies the advisers through their prior service.
verses.before: King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, “How do you counsel me to answer this people?”
verses.after: King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to answer these people?” he asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, “How do you counsel me to answer this people?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the servant/serve/servants reversal.
verses.before: They spoke to him, saying, “If today you will become a servant to this people, serve them, answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants always.”
verses.after: They answered, “If today you become a servant to these people and serve them, responding with good words, they will be your servants always.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They spoke to him, saying, “If today you will become a servant to this people, serve them, answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants always.”

verses.rationale: Keeps generational contrast without inventing their ages.
verses.before: But he abandoned the counsel that the elders had given him and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
verses.after: But he abandoned the elders’ advice and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he abandoned the counsel that the elders had given him and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated demand within consultation.
verses.before: He said to them, “What do you counsel, that we may answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke that your father placed upon us’?”
verses.after: He asked them, “What do you advise? How should we answer these people who have asked me, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “What do you counsel, that we may answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke that your father placed upon us’?”

verses.rationale: Uses traditional finger expansion with the Hebrew little-one ambiguity noted.
verses.before: The young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “This is what you should say to this people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy; but you, lighten it for us.’ This is what you should say to them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.
verses.after: The young men who had grown up with him answered, “Tell these people who said, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy; lighten it for us’: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
verses.tsw_comparator: The young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “This is what you should say to this people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy; but you, lighten it for us.’ This is what you should say to them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threat’s paired intensifications and scorpion image.
verses.before: And now, though my father loaded a heavy yoke upon you, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
verses.after: My father loaded you with a heavy yoke; I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, though my father loaded a heavy yoke upon you, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated appointment.
verses.before: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had said: “Return to me on the third day.”
verses.after: Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them: “Return to me on the third day.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had said: “Return to me on the third day.”

verses.rationale: Retains harshness and rejected counsel as narration.
verses.before: The king answered the people harshly, abandoning the counsel that the elders had given him.
verses.after: The king answered the people harshly. He abandoned the advice the elders had given him
verses.tsw_comparator: The king answered the people harshly, abandoning the counsel that the elders had given him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated threat but does not import the omitted finger boast.
verses.before: He spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”
verses.after: and spoke as the young men advised: “My father made your yoke heavy; I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with scorpions.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”

verses.rationale: Retains divine agency alongside the king’s refusal.
verses.before: So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from the LORD, in order to establish his word that the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
