verses.tsw_comparator: Asa lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David his father. Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keeps both synchronism and duration.
verses.before: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
verses.after: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah. He ruled Israel for two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

verses.rationale: Preserves inherited and induced wrongdoing.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in his sin, by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.after: He did evil in the LORD’s eyes, following his father’s way and the sin by which his father had led Israel into sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in his sin, by which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps tribal origin and the siege setting.
verses.before: Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him. Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
verses.after: Baasha son of Ahijah, from Issachar’s house, conspired against him. Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him. Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.

verses.rationale: Preserves murder and accession date.
verses.before: Baasha put him to death in the third year of Asa king of Judah and became king in his place.
verses.after: Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah and became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Baasha put him to death in the third year of Asa king of Judah and became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keeps total household destruction explicit.
verses.before: As soon as he became king, he struck down all the house of Jeroboam. He did not leave Jeroboam anyone who breathed, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
verses.after: As soon as he became king, he struck down Jeroboam’s whole house. He left Jeroboam no one breathing, destroying them all, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah of Shiloh.
verses.tsw_comparator: As soon as he became king, he struck down all the house of Jeroboam. He did not leave Jeroboam anyone who breathed, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s causal explanation.
verses.before: because of the sins of Jeroboam that he committed and by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
verses.after: This happened because of Jeroboam’s sins, which he committed and led Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, Israel’s God, to anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of the sins of Jeroboam that he committed and by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.

verses.rationale: Preserves the formula rather than omitting repetition.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Nadab’s history and all he did—are they not written in the Book of the Annals of Israel’s Kings?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Retains the exact repeated war notice.
verses.before: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
verses.after: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

verses.rationale: Preserves capital, accession and duration.
verses.before: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel at Tirzah, for twenty-four years.
verses.after: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel at Tirzah. He ruled twenty-four years.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel at Tirzah, for twenty-four years.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new dynasty’s continuation of the same sin.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.after: He did evil in the LORD’s eyes, following Jeroboam’s way and the sin by which Jeroboam had led Israel into sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, by which he caused Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Identifies this Jehu through his father and prophetic role.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani concerning Baasha, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani concerning Baasha, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves dust-to-leadership contrast.
verses.before: “Because I raised you up from the dust and made you leader over my people Israel, yet you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused my people Israel to sin, provoking me to anger by their sins,
verses.after: “I raised you from the dust and made you leader over my people Israel. But you followed Jeroboam’s way and led my people Israel into sin, provoking me to anger with their sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Because I raised you up from the dust and made you leader over my people Israel, yet you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused my people Israel to sin, provoking me to anger by their sins,

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from third-person Baasha to direct your.
verses.before: look, I will sweep away Baasha and his house. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.after: Now I will sweep away Baasha and his house. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.tsw_comparator: look, I will sweep away Baasha and his house. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated city/country judgment.
verses.before: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone belonging to him who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat.”
verses.after: Dogs will eat anyone of Baasha’s house who dies in the city, and the birds of the sky will eat anyone who dies in the open country.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone belonging to him who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat.”

verses.rationale: Keeps all annal categories.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha—what he did and his might—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Baasha’s history, what he did, and his mighty deeds—are they not written in the Book of the Annals of Israel’s Kings?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha—what he did and his might—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Preserves burial and succession.
verses.before: Baasha lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Baasha lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah. His son Elah became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Baasha lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Keeps the tension between fulfilling judgment and being judged for the slaughter.
verses.before: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through Jehu son of Hanani the prophet against Baasha and against his house, because of all the evil that he did in the sight of the LORD, provoking him to anger by the work of his hands, becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.
verses.after: The LORD’s word also came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he did in the LORD’s eyes, provoking him with the work of his hands and becoming like Jeroboam’s house—and because he struck that house down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through Jehu son of Hanani the prophet against Baasha and against his house, because of all the evil that he did in the sight of the LORD, provoking him to anger by the work of his hands, becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.

verses.rationale: Retains accession, capital and duration.
verses.before: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah for two years.
verses.after: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel at Tirzah. He ruled two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah for two years.

verses.rationale: Clarifies Elah as the drinker and Arza’s office.
verses.before: But his servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him. Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.
verses.after: His servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, conspired against him. Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who managed the palace there.
verses.tsw_comparator: But his servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him. Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.

verses.rationale: Keeps execution and regnal timing explicit.
verses.before: Zimri came in, struck him down, and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah; and he became king in his place.
verses.after: Zimri entered, struck him down, and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah. He became king in Elah’s place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zimri came in, struck him down, and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah; and he became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retains the coarse idiom and wider circle of victims.
verses.before: When he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he struck down all the house of Baasha. He did not leave him a single male, neither his kinsmen nor his friends.
verses.after: As soon as he became king and sat on the throne, he struck down Baasha’s whole house. He left him no male who urinates against a wall, no relative, and no friend.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he struck down all the house of Baasha. He did not leave him a single male, neither his kinsmen nor his friends.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fulfillment formula.
verses.before: Thus Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,
verses.after: Zimri destroyed Baasha’s whole house, just as the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,

verses.rationale: Keeps both generations and worthlessness language.
verses.before: because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned and by which they caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless things.
verses.after: because of all the sins of Baasha and his son Elah, which they committed and led Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, Israel’s God, with their worthless idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned and by which they caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless things.

verses.rationale: Retains the annal refrain.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Elah’s history and all he did—are they not written in the Book of the Annals of Israel’s Kings?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keeps the exceptionally brief reign and army location.
verses.before: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. Now the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
verses.after: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri ruled seven days in Tirzah. The troops were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. Now the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reported coup and immediate rival accession.
verses.before: The people who were encamped heard it said, “Zimri has conspired and has also struck down the king.” So all Israel made Omri, commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.
verses.after: The troops in camp heard, “Zimri has conspired and killed the king.” That very day, in the camp, all Israel made Omri, the army commander, king over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people who were encamped heard it said, “Zimri has conspired and has also struck down the king.” So all Israel made Omri, commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.

verses.rationale: Keeps the army’s shift of target.
verses.before: Omri went up from Gibbethon with all Israel, and they besieged Tirzah.
verses.after: Omri and all Israel with him left Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Omri went up from Gibbethon with all Israel, and they besieged Tirzah.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-initiated fatal fire without added motive.
verses.before: When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the citadel of the king’s house and burned the king’s house down over himself with fire, and he died,
verses.after: When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the citadel of the king’s house and set the palace on fire over himself. He died
verses.tsw_comparator: When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the citadel of the king’s house and burned the king’s house down over himself with fire, and he died,

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s causal evaluation across the verse boundary.
verses.before: because of his sins that he had committed, doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin that he had committed, causing Israel to sin.
verses.after: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the LORD’s eyes, following Jeroboam’s way and the sin by which he led Israel into sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of his sins that he had committed, doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin that he had committed, causing Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Retains conspiracy as the named annal subject.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy that he made, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Zimri’s history and the conspiracy he carried out—are they not written in the Book of the Annals of Israel’s Kings?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy that he made, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keeps both factions and the claimant’s patronymic.
verses.before: Then the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri.
verses.after: Then Israel’s people split in two. Half followed Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half followed Omri.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri.

verses.rationale: Does not invent the cause of Tibni’s death.
verses.before: But the people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri became king.
verses.after: Omri’s followers prevailed over the followers of Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri became king.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri became king.

verses.rationale: Preserves the second accession date and both durations.
verses.before: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel for twelve years. He reigned six years in Tirzah.
verses.after: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel. He ruled twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel for twelve years. He reigned six years in Tirzah.

verses.rationale: Keeps price and name explanation.
verses.before: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. He built on the hill and called the name of the city that he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill.
verses.after: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built on it. He named the city he built Samaria after Shemer, the hill’s owner.
verses.tsw_comparator: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. He built on the hill and called the name of the city that he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill.

verses.rationale: Retains the escalating evaluation.
verses.before: Omri did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and did more evil than everyone who were before him.
verses.after: Omri did evil in the LORD’s eyes, more evil than all who came before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Omri did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and did more evil than all who were before him.

verses.rationale: Follows singular read sin and keeps induced wrongdoing.
verses.before: He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless things.
verses.after: He followed Jeroboam son of Nebat in all his ways and in the sin by which he led Israel into sin, provoking the LORD, Israel’s God, with their worthless idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless things.

verses.rationale: Preserves the annal categories.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.after: The rest of Omri’s history, what he did, and the mighty deeds he accomplished—are they not written in the Book of the Annals of Israel’s Kings?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.rationale: Keeps the new burial capital and succession.
verses.before: Omri lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son became king in his place.
verses.after: Omri lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab became king in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Omri lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated full name and chronological data.
verses.before: Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah. Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
verses.after: Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah. Ahab son of Omri ruled Israel from Samaria for twenty-two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah. Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

verses.rationale: Preserves the further escalation.
verses.before: Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, more than everyone who were before him.
verses.after: Ahab son of Omri did more evil in the LORD’s eyes than all who came before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.

verses.rationale: Keeps Ahab’s actions and the named marriage alliance.
verses.before: As though it were a small thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
verses.after: As though following the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat were a small thing, he married Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians. He went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: As though it were a small thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.

verses.rationale: Retains altar, temple and capital.
verses.before: He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he had built in Samaria.
verses.after: He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal he built in Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he had built in Samaria.

verses.rationale: Keeps cult object and superlative judgment.
verses.before: Ahab also made the Asherah. Ahab went on doing more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.after: Ahab also made an Asherah pole. He did more to provoke the LORD, Israel’s God, than all the kings of Israel before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab also made the Asherah. Ahab went on doing more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sons’ loss without asserting an unmentioned sacrificial mechanism.
verses.before: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the LORD, which he spoke through Joshua son of Nun.
verses.after: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. He laid its foundations at the cost of Abiram his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of Segub his youngest, just as the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the LORD, which he spoke through Joshua son of Nun.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned inhabitant description and dew/rain oath.
verses.before: Elijah the Tishbite, from the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand: there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except by my word.”
verses.after: Elijah the Tishbite, one of the inhabitants of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD, Israel’s God, lives, whom I serve, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except at my word.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah the Tishbite, from the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand: there shall be neither dew nor rain in these years except by my word.”

verses.rationale: Retains the new divine instruction.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to him:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves direction and hiding place.
verses.before: “Go from here and turn eastward. Hide yourself by the Wadi Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.
verses.after: “Leave here, turn east, and hide by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go from here and turn eastward. Hide yourself by the Wadi Cherith, which is east of the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Keeps ravens rather than reinterpreting them as people.

verses.after: You will drink from the wadi. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to provide for you there.”

verses.rationale: Retains obedient action and repeated location.

verses.rationale: Preserves both repeated meals and water source.
verses.before: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.
verses.after: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening. He drank from the wadi.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prophet affected by the drought.

verses.after: After a time the wadi dried up, because no rain had fallen in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: After some time, the wadi dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated word formula.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.after: Then the word of the LORD came to him:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves foreign territory and widow’s role.

verses.after: “Get up and go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. I have commanded a widow there to feed you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Get up; go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and live there. Look, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the encounter and modest first request.

verses.after: He went to Zarephath. At the town’s entrance a widow was gathering sticks. He called to her, “Please bring me a little water in a vessel so I can drink.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the entrance of the city, there was a widow gathering sticks there. He called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a vessel, so that I may drink.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the additional demand while she is already moving.
verses.before: As she went to get it, he called after her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand.”
verses.after: As she went to get it, he called after her, “Please bring me a piece of bread too.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As she went to get it, he called after her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand.”

verses.rationale: Keeps her oath, scarcity and stark expectation of death.
verses.before: But she said, “As the LORD your God lives, I have no cake—only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug. Look, I am gathering two sticks, so that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son. We will eat it, and die.”
verses.after: She said, “As the LORD your God lives, I have no baked bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks to go and prepare it for myself and my son. We will eat it, and then we will die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But she said, “As the LORD your God lives, I have no cake—only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug. Look, I am gathering two sticks, so that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son. We will eat it, and die.”

verses.rationale: Retains the unsettling first claim on scarce food.
verses.before: Elijah said to her, “Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake from it and bring it out to me; afterward make something for yourself and your son.
verses.after: Elijah told her, “Do not be afraid. Go and do as you said. But first make me a small cake from it and bring it out to me. Afterward make something for yourself and your son.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said to her, “Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake from it and bring it out to me; afterward make something for yourself and your son.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two provisions and bounded duration.
verses.before: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: The jar of flour will not be used up, and the jug of oil will not fail, until the day the LORD gives rain upon the face of the ground.”
verses.after: For this is what the LORD, Israel’s God, says: ‘The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not fail, until the day the LORD sends rain on the ground.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: The jar of flour shall not be used up, and the jug of oil shall not fail, until the day the LORD gives rain upon the face of the ground.”

verses.rationale: Follows the read she/he order and includes household.
verses.before: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah. She ate—she and he and her household—for days.
verses.after: She went and did as Elijah said. She, he, and her household ate for many days.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah. She ate—she and he and her household—for days.

verses.rationale: Preserves the promise’s repeated wording.
verses.before: The jar of flour was not used up, and the jug of oil did not fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke through Elijah.
verses.after: The jar of flour did not run out, and the jug of oil did not fail, just as the LORD had said through Elijah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The jar of flour was not used up, and the jug of oil did not fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke through Elijah.

verses.rationale: Retains the woman’s household role and the absence of breath.
verses.before: After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill. His illness became very severe, until no breath remained in him.
verses.after: After this, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. His illness grew so severe that no breath remained in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill. His illness became very severe, until no breath remained in him.

verses.rationale: Keeps accusation as the grieving woman’s question.
verses.before: She said to Elijah, “What is there between me and you, man of God? Have you come to me to bring my guilt to remembrance and to put my son to death?”
verses.after: She said to Elijah, “What have you to do with me, man of God? Have you come to bring my guilt to mind and kill my son?”
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to Elijah, “What is there between me and you, man of God? Have you come to me to bring my guilt to remembrance and to put my son to death?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the physical movement and upper-room setting.
verses.before: He said to her, “Give me your son.” He took him from her arms, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
verses.after: “Give me your son,” he said. He took him from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to her, “Give me your son.” He took him from her arms, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.

verses.rationale: Does not soften Elijah’s accusation toward God.
verses.before: Then he cried out to the LORD and said, “LORD, my God, have you also brought harm upon the widow with whom I am staying, by putting her son to death?”
verses.after: He cried to the LORD, “LORD my God, have you brought disaster even on this widow with whom I am staying, by killing her son?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he cried out to the LORD and said, “LORD, my God, have you also brought harm upon the widow with whom I am staying, by putting her son to death?”

verses.rationale: Retains bodily action, count and returning life without a doctrinal gloss.
verses.before: He stretched himself over the child three times, and cried out to the LORD, saying, “LORD, my God, please let the life of this child return within him.”
verses.after: He stretched himself over the child three times and cried to the LORD, “LORD my God, please let this child’s life return into him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He stretched himself over the child three times, and cried out to the LORD, saying, “LORD, my God, please let the life of this child return within him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing and restored life in sequence.
verses.before: The LORD listened to Elijah’s voice, and the life of the child returned within him, and he lived.
verses.after: The LORD heard Elijah’s voice. The child’s life returned into him, and he lived.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD listened to Elijah’s voice, and the life of the child returned within him, and he lived.

verses.rationale: Preserves return to the mother and direct announcement.
verses.before: Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, “See—your son lives.”
verses.after: Elijah took the child down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother. “Look,” he said, “your son is alive.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. Elijah said, “See—your son lives.”

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition and word-in-mouth imagery.
verses.before: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.”
verses.after: The woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the LORD’s word in your mouth is true.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.”

verses.rationale: Preserves third year without importing another duration.
verses.before: After many days, the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, “Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon the face of the land.”
verses.after: After a long time, in the third year, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: “Go, show yourself to Ahab. I will send rain on the ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: After many days, the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, “Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon the face of the land.”

verses.rationale: Keeps response and famine setting.
verses.before: So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. Now the famine was severe in Samaria.
verses.after: Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine in Samaria was severe.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. Now the famine was severe in Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retains royal service alongside devotion to the LORD.
verses.before: Ahab called Obadiah, who was over the household. Now Obadiah greatly feared the LORD.
verses.after: Ahab summoned Obadiah, who managed the palace. Obadiah deeply feared the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab called Obadiah, who was over the household. Now Obadiah greatly feared the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps killing, protection, counts and provisions.
verses.before: For when Jezebel was cutting off the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men in each cave, and sustained them with bread and water.
verses.after: When Jezebel was cutting down the LORD’s prophets, Obadiah had hidden a hundred of them in caves, fifty to a cave, and supplied them with bread and water.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when Jezebel was cutting off the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men in each cave, and sustained them with bread and water.

verses.rationale: Retains the animal-preservation concern and uncertain loss/destruction sense.
verses.before: Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go through the land, to all the springs of water and to all the wadis. Perhaps we may find grass and keep horse and mule alive, so that we will not have to destroy some of the livestock.”
verses.after: Ahab told Obadiah, “Go through the land to every spring and every wadi. Perhaps we can find grass and keep the horses and mules alive, so we will not have to destroy any of the animals.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go through the land, to all the springs of water and to all the wadis. Perhaps we may find grass and keep horse and mule alive, so that we will not have to destroy some of the livestock.”

verses.rationale: Keeps separate routes and repeated solitude.
verses.before: So they divided the land between them to pass through it. Ahab went by one way by himself, and Obadiah went by another way by himself.
verses.after: They divided the land between them to search it. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah another.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they divided the land between them to pass through it. Ahab went by one way by himself, and Obadiah went by another way by himself.

verses.rationale: Retains recognition and bodily deference.
verses.before: As Obadiah was on the way, there was Elijah coming toward him. He recognized him and fell upon his face, and said, “Is this you, my lord Elijah?”
verses.after: As Obadiah went along, Elijah met him. He recognized him, fell facedown, and said, “Is it really you, my lord Elijah?”
verses.tsw_comparator: As Obadiah was on the way, there was Elijah coming toward him. He recognized him and fell upon his face, and said, “Is this you, my lord Elijah?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrasting my/your lord dialogue.
verses.before: He said to him, “It is I. Go, tell your lord, ‘Elijah is here.’”
verses.after: “It is,” he replied. “Go, tell your lord, ‘Elijah is here.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “It is I. Go, tell your lord, ‘Elijah is here.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the fearful accusation as a question.
verses.before: But he said, “What sin have I committed, that you are giving your servant into Ahab’s hand to kill me?
verses.after: Obadiah said, “What sin have I committed that you would hand your servant over to Ahab to kill me?
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, “What sin have I committed, that you are giving your servant into Ahab’s hand to kill me?

verses.rationale: Retains the oath and universal search claim.
verses.before: As the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he made the kingdom and nation swear that they could not find you.
verses.after: As the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to look for you. Whenever they said, ‘He is not here,’ he made that kingdom or nation swear they could not find you.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he made the kingdom and nation swear that they could not find you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first repeated protest.
verses.before: And now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Elijah is here.”’
verses.after: And now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Elijah is here.”’
verses.tsw_comparator: And now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Elijah is here.”’

verses.rationale: Keeps the feared Spirit action hypothetical.
verses.before: And when I go from you, the spirit of the LORD may carry you where I do not know. Then I will come and tell Ahab, and he will not find you, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has feared the LORD from my youth.
verses.after: As soon as I leave you, the LORD’s Spirit may carry you somewhere I do not know. If I tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will kill me. Yet your servant has feared the LORD since my youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when I go from you, the spirit of the LORD may carry you where I do not know. Then I will come and tell Ahab, and he will not find you, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has feared the LORD from my youth.

verses.rationale: Retains the full retelling of protective action.
verses.before: Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the LORD—how I hid a hundred men of the prophets of the LORD, fifty men in each cave, and sustained them with bread and water?
verses.after: Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel killed the LORD’s prophets? I hid a hundred of the LORD’s prophets in caves, fifty to a cave, and supplied them with bread and water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the LORD—how I hid a hundred men of the prophets of the LORD, fifty men in each cave, and sustained them with bread and water?

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated protest and lethal fear.
verses.before: And now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Elijah is here,”’ and he will kill me.”
verses.after: And now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Elijah is here.”’ He will kill me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Elijah is here,”’ and he will kill me.”

verses.rationale: Retains the oath’s title and today assurance.
verses.before: Elijah said, “As the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, today I will surely show myself to him.”
verses.after: Elijah said, “As the LORD of Armies lives, whom I serve, I will show myself to Ahab today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said, “As the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, today I will surely show myself to him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the two meetings in sequence.
verses.before: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. Then Ahab went to meet Elijah.
verses.after: Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. Then Ahab went to meet Elijah.

verses.rationale: Makes the accusation natural while preserving trouble language.
verses.before: When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, “Is this you, troubler of Israel?”
verses.after: When Ahab saw Elijah, he said, “Is that you, the one bringing trouble on Israel?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, “Is this you, troubler of Israel?”

verses.rationale: Retains reversal of blame and plural Baals.
verses.before: He said, “I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father’s house have, by forsaking the commandments of the LORD and following the Baals.
verses.after: Elijah answered, “I have not brought trouble on Israel. You and your father’s house have, by abandoning the LORD’s commands and following the Baals.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father’s house have, by forsaking the commandments of the LORD and following the Baals.

verses.rationale: Keeps both prophetic groups and patronage.
verses.before: Now send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel’s table.”
verses.after: Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel, along with Baal’s four hundred fifty prophets and Asherah’s four hundred prophets, who eat at Jezebel’s table.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel’s table.”

verses.rationale: Retains the response without adding attendance details for each group.
verses.before: So Ahab sent throughout all the people of Israel and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.
verses.after: Ahab sent throughout Israel and assembled the prophets on Mount Carmel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Ahab sent throughout all the people of Israel and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the limping image and collective silence.
verses.before: Then Elijah came near to all the people and said, “How long will you limp between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, follow him.” But the people did not answer him a word.
verses.after: Elijah approached all the people and said, “How long will you limp between two sides? If the LORD is God, follow him. If Baal is, follow him.” The people answered him not a word.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Elijah came near to all the people and said, “How long will you limp between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, follow him.” But the people did not answer him a word.

verses.rationale: Leaves alone as Elijah’s claim beside Obadiah’s preserved prophets.
verses.before: Then Elijah said to the people, “I alone remain as a prophet of the LORD, while the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men.
verses.after: Then Elijah said, “I alone remain as a prophet of the LORD, but Baal has four hundred fifty prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Elijah said to the people, “I alone remain as a prophet of the LORD, while the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men.

verses.rationale: Preserves both preparations and repeated prohibition.
verses.before: Let them give us two bulls. Let them choose one bull for themselves, cut it into pieces, and place it on the wood—but they must put no fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and place it on the wood, and I will put no fire to it.
verses.after: Let two bulls be brought to us. Let them choose one, cut it up, and place it on the wood, but light no fire. I will prepare the other bull and place it on the wood, and I will light no fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them give us two bulls. Let them choose one bull for themselves, cut it into pieces, and place it on the wood—but they must put no fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and place it on the wood, and I will put no fire to it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the agreed criterion and Name contrast.
verses.before: Then you will call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers by fire—that one is God.” All the people answered and said, “The word is good.”
verses.after: You call on your god’s name, and I will call on the LORD’s name. The God who answers with fire is God.” All the people answered, “That is good.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers by fire—that one is God.” All the people answered and said, “The word is good.”

verses.rationale: Retains their priority and repeated instruction.
verses.before: Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, “Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, because you are the many. Call on the name of your god, but put no fire to it.”
verses.after: Elijah told Baal’s prophets, “Choose one bull and prepare it first, since there are so many of you. Call on your god’s name, but light no fire.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, “Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, because you are the many. Call on the name of your god, but put no fire to it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves limping’s echo and the first no-answer refrain.
verses.before: So they took the bull that was given to them and prepared it. They called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, “Baal, answer us!” But there was no voice and no one answering. And they limped about the altar that had been made.
verses.after: They took the bull given to them and prepared it. From morning until noon they called on Baal’s name: “Baal, answer us!” But there was no voice, no answer. They limped around the altar that had been made.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they took the bull that was given to them and prepared it. They called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, “Baal, answer us!” But there was no voice and no one answering. And they limped about the altar that had been made.

verses.rationale: Keeps mockery and the possible bodily euphemism with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: At noon Elijah mocked them, saying, “Call out loudly, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or he has gone aside, or he is on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened.”
verses.after: At noon Elijah mocked them: “Call louder! He is a god, after all. Perhaps he is thinking, or relieving himself, or away on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep and must wake up.”
verses.tsw_comparator: At noon Elijah mocked them, saying, “Call out loudly, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or he has gone aside, or he is on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened.”

verses.rationale: Retains real bodily harm without expanding it.
verses.before: So they called out loudly and cut themselves, according to their custom, with swords and spears, until blood poured out upon them.
verses.after: They shouted louder and cut themselves with swords and spears, as was their custom, until blood poured over them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they called out loudly and cut themselves, according to their custom, with swords and spears, until blood poured out upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps prophetic terminology and the threefold failed response.
verses.before: When noon had passed, they raved on until the time of the offering of the grain offering. But there was no voice, no one answering, and no one paying attention.
verses.after: After noon they continued prophesying until the time of the offering. But there was no voice, no answer, no one paying attention.
verses.tsw_comparator: When noon had passed, they raved on until the time of the offering of the grain offering. But there was no voice, no one answering, and no one paying attention.

verses.rationale: Keeps gathering and restoration of the altar.
verses.before: Then Elijah said to all the people, “Come near to me.” So all the people came near to him. And he repaired the ruined altar of the LORD.
verses.after: Elijah told all the people, “Come closer to me.” They came, and he repaired the LORD’s altar, which had been torn down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Elijah said to all the people, “Come near to me.” So all the people came near to him. And he repaired the ruined altar of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves twelve tribes and the renaming link.
verses.before: Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD came, saying, “Israel will be your name.”
verses.after: Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of Jacob’s sons—Jacob, to whom the LORD had said, “Your name will be Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD came, saying, “Israel shall be your name.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the seed measure without assuming a geometric conversion.
verses.before: With the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD. Then he made a trench around the altar, large enough for two seahs of seed.
verses.after: With the stones he built an altar in the LORD’s name. Around it he made a trench large enough to hold two seahs of seed.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD. Then he made a trench around the altar, large enough for two seahs of seed.

verses.rationale: Follows this original Hebrew record’s contents; water command remains in the next record.
verses.before: He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and placed it on the wood.
verses.after: He arranged the wood, cut up the bull, and laid it on the wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and placed it on the wood.

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete water command with its original Hebrew verse binding.
verses.before: Then he said, “Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood.” Then he said, “Do it a second time.” And they did it a second time. Then he said, “Do it a third time.” And they did it a third time.
verses.after: He said, “Fill four jars with water and pour it over the burnt offering and the wood.” Then he said, “Do it again.” They did it again. “A third time,” he said, and they did it a third time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood.” Then he said, “Do it a second time.” And they did it a second time. Then he said, “Do it a third time.” And they did it a third time.

verses.rationale: Retains both overflow and filled trench.
verses.before: The water ran all around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.
verses.after: The water ran around the altar, and he filled the trench with water too.
verses.tsw_comparator: The water ran all around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.

verses.rationale: Retains Israel rather than substituting Jacob and follows singular read word.
verses.before: At the time when the grain offering was offered, Elijah the prophet came near and said, “LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that at your word I have done all these things.
verses.after: At the time of the offering, Elijah the prophet approached and said, “LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that I have done all this at your word.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the time when the grain offering was offered, Elijah the prophet came near and said, “LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that at your word I have done all these things.

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled petition and consequential heart-turning ambiguity in a note.
verses.before: Answer me, LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that you, LORD, are God, and that you have turned their heart back.”
verses.after: Answer me, LORD, answer me, so these people may know that you, LORD, are God, and that you have turned their hearts back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Answer me, LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that you, LORD, are God, and that you have turned their heart back.”

verses.rationale: Preserves every consumed element and licking image.
verses.before: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust; and it licked up the water that was in the trench.
verses.after: Then the LORD’s fire fell. It consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust; and it licked up the water that was in the trench.

verses.rationale: Retains the doubled confession.
verses.before: When all the people saw it, they fell upon their faces and said, “The LORD—he is God! The LORD—he is God!”
verses.after: When all the people saw it, they fell facedown and said, “The LORD is God! The LORD is God!”
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the people saw it, they fell upon their faces and said, “The LORD—he is God! The LORD—he is God!”

verses.rationale: Keeps Elijah’s agency and slaughter explicit.
verses.before: Elijah said to them, “Seize the prophets of Baal. Let not one of them escape!” So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.
verses.after: Elijah told them, “Seize Baal’s prophets! Do not let one escape.” They seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elijah said to them, “Seize the prophets of Baal. Let not one of them escape!” So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.

verses.rationale: Retains the announcement before the visible cloud.
verses.before: Then Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the roar of rain.”
verses.after: Then Elijah told Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink. There is the sound of heavy rain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the roar of rain.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrasting actions and unusual bodily posture.
verses.before: So Ahab went up to eat and drink, while Elijah went up to the top of Carmel. He bent down to the earth and put his face between his knees.
verses.after: Ahab went up to eat and drink. Elijah climbed to Carmel’s summit, bent down to the ground, and put his face between his knees.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Ahab went up to eat and drink, while Elijah went up to the top of Carmel. He bent down to the earth and put his face between his knees.

verses.rationale: Preserves repetition and lack of sight.
verses.before: He said to his servant, “Go up now; look toward the sea.” So he went up, looked, and said, “There is nothing.” Then he said, “Go back seven times.”
verses.after: He told his servant, “Go up and look toward the sea.” The servant looked and said, “There is nothing.” Seven times Elijah told him, “Go back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to his servant, “Go up now; look toward the sea.” So he went up, looked, and said, “There is nothing.” Then he said, “Go back seven times.”

verses.rationale: Keeps seventh observation and hand-sized cloud.
verses.before: On the seventh time he said, “Look, a small cloud, like a person’s palm, is rising from the sea.” Then he said, “Go up. Say to Ahab, ‘Harness your chariot and go down, so that the rain does not stop you.’”
verses.after: On the seventh time the servant said, “A cloud as small as a man’s hand is rising from the sea.” Elijah said, “Go, tell Ahab, ‘Harness your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: On the seventh time he said, “Look, a small cloud, like a person’s palm, is rising from the sea.” Then he said, “Go up. Say to Ahab, ‘Harness your chariot and go down, so that the rain does not stop you.’”

verses.rationale: Retains the changing weather and destination.
verses.before: And in a little while, the skies grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain. Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.
verses.after: In a little while the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and heavy rain fell. Ahab rode away to Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in a little while, the skies grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain. Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Makes girding practical while retaining divine hand imagery.
verses.before: The hand of the LORD was upon Elijah. He girded up his waist and ran before Ahab as far as the entrance to Jezreel.
verses.after: The LORD’s hand came upon Elijah. He tucked his clothing into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to the entrance of Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hand of the LORD was upon Elijah. He girded up his waist and ran before Ahab as far as the entrance to Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the report’s violence and scope.
verses.before: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and all about how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
verses.after: Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and all about how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-curse, deadline and threatened death.

verses.after: Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: “May the gods do this to me, and more besides, if by this time tomorrow I have not made your life like the life of one of them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “May the gods do so to me, and more also, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the life of one of them.”

verses.rationale: Follows pinned saw rather than feared, retaining flight for life.
verses.before: He saw it, rose up, and went for his life. He came to Beer-sheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.
verses.after: When he saw this, he got up and went for his life. He reached Beer-sheba in Judah and left his servant there.
verses.tsw_comparator: He saw it, rose up, and went for his life. He came to Beer-sheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.

verses.rationale: Keeps the death wish and comparison without psychologizing.
verses.before: But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness. He came and sat down beneath a broom tree. He asked that he might die, saying, “Enough now, LORD. Take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors.”
verses.after: He himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness and sat under a broom bush. He asked to die: “Enough now, LORD. Take my life. I am no better than my ancestors.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness. He came and sat down beneath a broom tree. He asked that he might die, saying, “Enough now, LORD. Take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors.”

verses.rationale: Retains sleep, touch and practical instruction.
verses.before: Then he lay down and slept beneath the broom tree. And look: an angel was touching him and said to him, “Get up. Eat.”
verses.after: He lay down and slept under the broom bush. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he lay down and slept beneath the broom tree. And look: an angel was touching him and said to him, “Get up. Eat.”

verses.rationale: Preserves food, water and renewed rest.
verses.before: He looked, and there at his head was a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank, then lay down again.
verses.after: He looked, and there beside his head were a cake baked on hot stones and a jug of water. He ate and drank, then lay down again.
verses.tsw_comparator: He looked, and there at his head was a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank, then lay down again.

verses.rationale: Keeps the second touch and acknowledged limitation.

verses.after: The LORD’s angel came back a second time, touched him, and said, “Get up and eat. The journey is too much for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The angel of the LORD came back a second time, touched him, and said, “Get up. Eat, for the journey is too much for you.”

verses.rationale: Retains both forty counts and destination’s sacred name.

verses.after: He got up, ate, and drank. Strengthened by that food, he traveled forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he got up, ate, and drank. In the strength of that food he went forty days and forty nights, as far as Horeb, the mountain of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the definite cave without inventing its identity.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three accusations and subjective alone claim.

verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking my life to take it.”

verses.rationale: Retains command, destructive forces and repeated divine absence.

A great and powerful wind was tearing apart mountains and breaking rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
verses.after: He said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.” The LORD was passing by. A great, powerful wind tore mountains apart and shattered rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.” And look: the LORD was passing by. A great and powerful wind was tearing apart mountains and breaking rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paradoxical sound/stillness expression with alternatives in a note.
verses.before: After the earthquake came fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire came a sound of thin silence.
verses.after: After the earthquake came fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire came a sound of fine stillness.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the earthquake came fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire came a sound of thin silence.

verses.rationale: Keeps the delayed exit and repeated question.

verses.after: He answered, “I have been intensely zealous for the LORD, the God of Armies. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone remain, and they are seeking my life to take it.”

verses.rationale: Keeps destination and first commission.

verses.rationale: Preserves both remaining appointments and full identifiers.

verses.after: Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah as prophet in your place.

verses.rationale: Does not soften the lethal commission or explain its later realization.

verses.rationale: Keeps remnant number and bodily acts of allegiance.
verses.before: “But I will leave seven thousand in Israel: every knee that has not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”
verses.after: Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel: every knee that has not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the twelve teams and cloak action.

verses.rationale: Retains the parents and Elijah’s open-ended question.

verses.after: Elisha left the cattle and ran after Elijah. “Please let me kiss my father and mother,” he said, “and then I will follow you.” Elijah answered, “Go back. What have I done to you?”

verses.rationale: Keeps farewell meal and destroyed equipment without adding a sermon.

verses.after: Elisha turned back, took his pair of cattle, and slaughtered them. Using the cattle’s equipment as fuel, he boiled the meat and gave it to the people to eat. Then he got up, followed Elijah, and served him.

verses.rationale: Preserves coalition count and military sequence.

verses.after: Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army, with thirty-two kings, horses, and chariots. He advanced on Samaria, besieged it, and attacked it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his army, with thirty-two kings allied with him, horses, and chariots. He went up, laid siege to Samaria, and fought against it.

verses.rationale: Keeps this original source record’s messenger action.
verses.before: He sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel
verses.after: He sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel

verses.rationale: Places the whole demand in its Hebrew-bound verse and retains seizure of people.

verses.after: His message was: “This is what Ben-hadad says: Your silver and gold are mine. Your wives and your finest sons are mine too.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to him, “Thus says Ben-hadad: ‘Your silver and your gold are mine; your wives also and your finest children are mine.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps submission and its full scope.
verses.before: The king of Israel answered, “According to your word, my lord the king: I am yours, with all that is mine.”
verses.after: The king of Israel answered, “As you say, my lord the king. I and all I have are yours.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel answered, “According to your word, my lord the king: I am yours, with all that is mine.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated initial demand.
verses.before: The messengers returned and said, “Thus says Ben-hadad: ‘I sent to you, saying, “You must give me your silver and your gold, your wives and your children.”
verses.after: The messengers returned and said, “This is what Ben-hadad says: I sent word that you must give me your silver, gold, wives, and sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messengers returned and said, “Thus says Ben-hadad: ‘I sent to you, saying, “You must give me your silver and your gold, your wives and your children.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the expanded search and your-eyes reading.
verses.before: But about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you. They will search your house and the houses of your servants, and whatever is desirable in your eyes they will put in their hands and take away.’”
verses.after: But about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you. They will search your house and your servants’ houses. Whatever is precious in your eyes, they will seize and carry away.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you. They will search your house and the houses of your servants, and whatever is desirable in your eyes they will put in their hands and take away.’”

verses.rationale: Retains Ahab’s report of compliance and escalated threat.
verses.before: Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, “Please consider and see that this man is seeking harm. For he sent for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I did not withhold them from him.”
verses.after: The king of Israel summoned all the land’s elders. “Please take note,” he said. “See how this man seeks our harm. He demanded my wives, sons, silver, and gold, and I did not refuse him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, “Please consider and see that this man is seeking harm. For he sent for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I did not withhold them from him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps joint opposition and paired refusal.
verses.before: All the elders and all the people said to him, “Do not listen, and do not consent.”
verses.after: All the elders and all the people said, “Do not listen to him or agree.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the elders and all the people said to him, “Do not listen, and do not consent.”

verses.rationale: Preserves limited refusal rather than total repudiation.

verses.after: He told Ben-hadad’s messengers, “Tell my lord the king: I will do everything you first asked of your servant, but I cannot do this.” The messengers left and took back his answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he said to Ben-hadad’s messengers, “Say to my lord the king, ‘Everything that you first demanded of your servant I will do, but this thing I cannot do.’” The messengers went and brought him word again.

verses.rationale: Keeps the boast’s dust image and self-curse.

verses.after: Ben-hadad sent back this message: “May the gods do this to me, and more besides, if Samaria’s dust is enough to give a handful to each of the people following me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-hadad sent word to him and said, “May the gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for handfuls for all the people who follow me.”

verses.rationale: Makes the proverb’s implied equipment explicit.

verses.after: The king of Israel answered, “Tell him: Someone putting on armor should not boast like someone taking it off.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel answered, “Tell him: ‘Let not one who puts on armor boast like one who takes it off.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps drinking and the attack preparation.

verses.after: Ben-hadad heard this while he and the kings were drinking in their shelters. He ordered his servants, “Take your positions!” They took their positions against the city.

verses.rationale: Retains victory’s stated revelatory purpose.

verses.after: A prophet approached Ahab king of Israel and said, “This is what the LORD says: Do you see this great army? I am giving it into your hand today, and you will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a prophet came near to Ahab king of Israel and said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Have you seen all this great multitude? Look, I am giving it into your hand today, and you will know that I am the LORD.’”

verses.rationale: Makes alternating speakers clear without changing the unusual force.
verses.before: Ahab said, “By whom?” He said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘By the young men of the provincial commanders.’” Then he said, “Who will begin the battle?” He said, “You.”
verses.after: “Through whom?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The LORD says: Through the young attendants of the district commanders.” “Who is to begin the battle?” Ahab asked. “You,” he replied.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab said, “By whom?” He said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘By the young men of the provincial commanders.’” Then he said, “Who will begin the battle?” He said, “You.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both force counts.

verses.after: Ahab mustered the district commanders’ young attendants: two hundred thirty-two. After them he mustered all the troops, all the Israelites: seven thousand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he mustered the young men of the provincial commanders: they were two hundred and thirty-two. After them he mustered all the people, all the people of Israel: seven thousand.

verses.rationale: Keeps time, intoxication and repeated coalition number.

verses.after: They went out at noon while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the shelters with the thirty-two kings who supported him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went out at noon, while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the shelters, he and the thirty-two kings who were helping him.

verses.tsw_comparator: The young men of the provincial commanders went out first. Ben-hadad sent out scouts, and they reported to him, “Men have come out from Samaria.”

verses.rationale: Retains the identical command for both possibilities.

verses.rationale: Preserves individual fighting and the king’s escape.
