verses.rationale: Keeps the warning’s realized timing.
verses.before: At the turn of the year Ben-hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
verses.after: At the turn of the year Ben-hadad mustered Aram and advanced to Aphek to fight Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the turn of the year Ben-hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the striking unequal-armies simile.
verses.before: The people of Israel were mustered and provisioned, and they went out to meet them. The people of Israel camped opposite them like two little flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.
verses.after: The Israelites were mustered and supplied, and went out to meet them. Israel camped opposite them like two little flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people of Israel were mustered and provisioned, and they went out to meet them. The people of Israel camped opposite them like two little flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the challenge to geographic divine limitation and plural final knowledge.
verses.before: Then a man of God came near and spoke to the king of Israel, saying, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Because Aram has said, “the LORD is a god of the hills, but not a god of the valleys,” I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD.’”
verses.after: The man of God approached the king of Israel and said, “This is what the LORD says: Because Aram has said, ‘The LORD is a god of the hills, not a god of the valleys,’ I will give this whole great army into your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a man of God came near and spoke to the king of Israel, saying, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Because Aram has said, “the LORD is a god of the hills, but not a god of the valleys,” I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves all three time/count details.
verses.before: They camped opposite one another for seven days. On the seventh day the battle drew near, and the people of Israel struck down one hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
verses.after: They camped opposite one another for seven days. On the seventh day battle began, and the Israelites struck down a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
verses.tsw_comparator: They camped opposite one another for seven days. On the seventh day the battle drew near, and the people of Israel struck down one hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wall disaster and royal hiding place.
verses.before: People who remained fled to Aphek, into the city; and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the remaining men. Ben-hadad fled and entered the city, into an inner room.
verses.after: The survivors fled into Aphek, where the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the remaining men. Ben-hadad fled into the city and hid in an inner room.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who remained fled to Aphek, into the city; and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the remaining men. Ben-hadad fled and entered the city, into an inner room.

verses.rationale: Preserves submission clothing and your life rather than changing it to ours.
verses.before: His servants said to him, “Look, please, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of steadfast love. Let us, please, put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will let you live.”
verses.after: His servants said, “We have heard that the kings of Israel’s house show mercy. Let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will spare your life.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His servants said to him, “Look, please, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of steadfast love. Let us, please, put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will let you live.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the unexpected brother designation.
verses.before: So they fastened sackcloth around their waists and ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel. They said, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please let me live.’” He said, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”
verses.after: They tied sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads and went to the king of Israel. “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please spare my life,’” they told him. Ahab answered, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they fastened sackcloth around their waists and ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel. They said, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please let me live.’” He said, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”

verses.rationale: Makes the word-catching idiom and changing agents readable.
verses.before: The men took this as an omen and quickly seized on it from him. They said, “Your brother Ben-hadad.” He said, “Come, bring him.” Ben-hadad came out to him, and Ahab had him come up into the chariot.
verses.after: The men took this as a favorable sign and quickly seized on his words. “Your brother Ben-hadad!” they said. “Go and bring him,” Ahab replied. Ben-hadad came out to him, and Ahab brought him up into his chariot.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men took this as an omen and quickly seized on it from him. They said, “Your brother Ben-hadad.” He said, “Come, bring him.” Ben-hadad came out to him, and Ahab had him come up into the chariot.

verses.rationale: Identifies speakers at the unmarked shift; commercial streets interpretation noted.
verses.before: Ben-hadad said to him, “The cities that my father took from your father I will restore. You may establish streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father established them in Samaria.” Ahab said, “On the basis of a covenant, I will send you away.” So he made a covenant with him and sent him away.
verses.after: Ben-hadad said, “I will return the towns my father took from your father. You may establish trading streets in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria.” Ahab answered, “On this covenant I will release you.” He made a covenant with him and let him go.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-hadad said to him, “The cities that my father took from your father I will restore. You may establish streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father established them in Samaria.” Ahab said, “On the basis of a covenant, I will send you away.” So he made a covenant with him and sent him away.

verses.rationale: Retains the prophetic group and disturbing command.
verses.before: Now one man from among the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the LORD, “Please strike me.” But the man refused to strike him.
verses.after: At the LORD’s word, one of the prophets’ company said to his companion, “Please strike me.” But the man refused.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now one man from among the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the LORD, “Please strike me.” But the man refused to strike him.

verses.rationale: Preserves judgment for refusing harm without explaining it away.
verses.before: Then he said to him, “Because you have not listened to the voice of the LORD, look, when you leave me, a lion will strike you.” When he left him, a lion found him and struck him down.
verses.after: He told him, “Because you did not listen to the LORD’s voice, a lion will strike you when you leave me.” When the man left, a lion met him and struck him down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to him, “Because you have not listened to the voice of the LORD, look, when you leave me, a lion will strike you.” When he left him, a lion found him and struck him down.

verses.rationale: Keeps injury as the actual response.
verses.before: Then he found another man and said, “Please strike me.” So the man struck him, striking and wounding him.
verses.after: The prophet found another man and said, “Please strike me.” The man struck him and wounded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he found another man and said, “Please strike me.” So the man struck him, striking and wounding him.

verses.rationale: Retains the disguise’s material and location.
verses.before: The prophet went and stood waiting for the king along the road. He disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.
verses.after: Then the prophet went and waited for the king beside the road, disguised with a bandage over his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prophet went and stood waiting for the king along the road. He disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps the enacted story’s two alternative penalties.
verses.before: As the king was passing by, he cried out to the king and said, “Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and look, a man turned aside and brought a man to me. He said, ‘Guard this man. If he should be missing, then your life will be for his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.’
verses.after: As the king passed, he cried out, “Your servant went into the thick of battle. A man turned aside and brought me another man, saying, ‘Guard this man. If he goes missing, your life will be for his life, or you must pay a talent of silver.’
verses.tsw_comparator: As the king was passing by, he cried out to the king and said, “Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and look, a man turned aside and brought a man to me. He said, ‘Guard this man. If he should be missing, then your life shall be for his life, or you shall weigh out a talent of silver.’

verses.rationale: Preserves self-judgment through the story.
verses.before: But while your servant was busy here and there, he was gone.” The king of Israel said to him, “So is your judgment; you yourself have decided it.”
verses.after: But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared.” The king of Israel told him, “That is your sentence. You have decided it yourself.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But while your servant was busy here and there, he was gone.” The king of Israel said to him, “So is your judgment; you yourself have decided it.”

verses.rationale: Keeps recognition after disguise removal.
verses.before: Then he quickly removed the bandage from over his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized that he was one of the prophets.
verses.after: The prophet quickly removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he quickly removed the bandage from over his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized that he was one of the prophets.

verses.rationale: Retains destruction-ban language and substitution judgment.
verses.before: He said to him, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Because you have let go from your hand the man devoted to me for destruction, your life will be for his life, and your people for his people.’”
verses.after: He told the king, “This is what the LORD says: Because you let the man I devoted to destruction escape from your hand, your life will be for his life, and your people for his people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Because you have let go from your hand the man devoted to me for destruction, your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the emotional pair repeated in the next chapter.
verses.before: The king of Israel went to his house sullen and troubled, and came to Samaria.
verses.after: The king of Israel went home to Samaria, sullen and angry.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel went to his house sullen and troubled, and came to Samaria.

verses.rationale: Retains owner, place and proximity.
verses.before: After these things, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.after: After these events, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: After these things, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

verses.rationale: Preserves both offered exchanges and the king’s purpose.
verses.before: Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard, so that it may be my vegetable garden, because it is near my house. I will give you a better vineyard in its place; or, if it is good in your eyes, I will give you its price in silver.”
verses.after: Ahab told Naboth, “Give me your vineyard for a vegetable garden, since it is close to my house. I will give you a better vineyard in exchange, or, if you prefer, pay you its value in silver.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard, so that it may be my vegetable garden, because it is near my house. I will give you a better vineyard in its place; or, if it is good in your eyes, I will give you its price in silver.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the LORD and ancestral inheritance as grounds for refusal.
verses.before: Yet Naboth said to Ahab, “May the LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my ancestors.”
verses.after: Naboth answered, “The LORD forbid that I give you my ancestors’ inheritance!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Naboth said to Ahab, “May the LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my ancestors.”

verses.rationale: Retains the emotional echo and bodily withdrawal.
verses.before: So Ahab went into his house sullen and angry because of the word Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, when he said, “I will not give you the inheritance of my ancestors.” He lay down on his bed, turned away his face, and would not eat bread.
verses.after: Ahab went home sullen and angry because Naboth the Jezreelite had said, “I will not give you my ancestors’ inheritance.” He lay on his bed, turned his face away, and would not eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Ahab went into his house sullen and angry because of the word Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, when he said, “I will not give you the inheritance of my ancestors.” He lay down on his bed, turned away his face, and would not eat bread.

verses.rationale: Keeps her question tied to his visible behavior.
verses.before: Then Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him, “Why is your spirit so sullen, that you are not eating bread?”
verses.after: His wife Jezebel came and asked, “Why are you so sullen that you will not eat?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him, “Why is your spirit so sullen, that you are not eating bread?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Ahab’s retelling, including its omission of ancestral inheritance.
verses.before: He said to her, “Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver; or, if you wish, I will give you a vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’”
verses.after: He told her, “I said to Naboth the Jezreelite, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver, or, if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in exchange.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to her, “Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver; or, if you wish, I will give you a vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps the royal challenge as a question, with alternative force noted.
verses.before: Jezebel his wife said to him, “Is this how you now exercise kingship over Israel? Get up, eat bread, and let your heart be glad. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.”
verses.after: His wife Jezebel said, “Are you now the one ruling Israel? Get up, eat, and cheer up. I will give you Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jezebel his wife said to him, “Is this how you now exercise kingship over Israel? Get up, eat bread, and let your heart be glad. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.”

verses.rationale: Preserves use of royal authority and local recipients.
verses.before: So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and the nobles who lived with Naboth in his city.
verses.after: She wrote letters in Ahab’s name and sealed them with his seal. She sent them to the elders and nobles living in Naboth’s town.
verses.tsw_comparator: So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and the nobles who lived with Naboth in his city.

verses.rationale: Keeps the religious assembly and prominent seat.
verses.before: She wrote in the letters, saying, “Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.after: In the letters she wrote, “Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: She wrote in the letters, saying, “Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth at the head of the people.

verses.rationale: Renders bless as the contextual euphemism curse, explicitly noted.
verses.before: Set two worthless men opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘You have cursed God and the king.’ Then bring him out and stone him, so that he dies.”
verses.after: Seat two worthless men opposite him and have them testify, ‘You cursed God and the king.’ Then take him out and stone him to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Set two worthless men opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘You have cursed God and the king.’ Then bring him out and stone him, so that he dies.”

verses.rationale: Retains local leaders’ agency and compliance.
verses.before: The people of his city—the elders and the nobles who lived in his city—did as Jezebel had sent word to them, according to what was written in the letters she had sent them.
verses.after: The men of Naboth’s town—the elders and nobles who lived there—did as Jezebel directed, just as she had written in her letters.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people of his city—the elders and the nobles who lived in his city—did as Jezebel had sent word to them, according to what was written in the letters she had sent them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the command’s exact enacted repetition.
verses.before: They proclaimed a fast and set Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.after: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: They proclaimed a fast and set Naboth at the head of the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps false testimony attributed and killing explicit.
verses.before: Then the two worthless men came in and sat opposite him. The worthless men testified against Naboth before the people, saying, “Naboth has cursed God and the king.” So they brought him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
verses.after: The two worthless men came and sat opposite him. Before the people they testified against Naboth: “Naboth cursed God and the king.” Then they took him outside the town and stoned him to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the two worthless men came in and sat opposite him. The worthless men testified against Naboth before the people, saying, “Naboth has cursed God and the king.” So they brought him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.

verses.rationale: Retains the death report’s two elements.
verses.before: Then they sent word to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”
verses.after: They sent word to Jezebel: “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they sent word to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”

verses.rationale: Keeps possession linked to death and its emphatic repetition.
verses.before: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, Jezebel said to Ahab, “Get up; take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, for Naboth is no longer alive but dead.”
verses.after: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she told Ahab, “Get up and take possession of the vineyard Naboth the Jezreelite refused to sell you. Naboth is no longer alive. He is dead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, Jezebel said to Ahab, “Get up; take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, for Naboth is no longer alive but dead.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Ahab’s direct participation in seizure.
verses.before: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
verses.after: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard to take possession of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.

verses.rationale: Retains divine intervention after dispossession.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

verses.rationale: Clarifies Samaria’s royal association while preserving vineyard location.
verses.before: “Get up; go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Look, he is in Naboth’s vineyard, where he has gone down to take possession of it.
verses.after: “Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who rules in Samaria. He is in Naboth’s vineyard, where he has gone to take possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Get up; go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Look, he is in Naboth’s vineyard, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

verses.rationale: Keeps murder accusation and place-specific blood judgment.
verses.before: You will speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: Have you murdered and also taken possession?’ Then you will speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: In the place where the dogs licked up Naboth’s blood, the dogs will lick up your blood—even yours.’”
verses.after: Tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered and also taken possession?’ Then tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: In the place where dogs licked Naboth’s blood, dogs will lick your blood—yours too.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: Have you murdered and also taken possession?’ Then you shall speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: In the place where the dogs licked up Naboth’s blood, the dogs will lick up your blood—even yours.’”

verses.rationale: Retains finding repetition and self-sale image.
verses.before: Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” And he said, “I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” “I have found you,” he answered, “because you have sold yourself to do evil in the LORD’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” And he said, “I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Marks the shift into divine first-person speech and retains coarse idiom.
verses.before: Look, I am bringing disaster upon you. I will sweep away after you and cut off from Ahab every male, whether bound or free in Israel.
verses.after: He says, ‘I am bringing disaster on you. I will sweep away your descendants and cut off every one of Ahab’s males who urinates against a wall, confined or free in Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am bringing disaster upon you. I will sweep away after you and cut off from Ahab every male, whether bound or free in Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps both earlier dynasties as precedents.
verses.before: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked me and caused Israel to sin.
verses.after: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you provoked me to anger and led Israel into sin.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked me and caused Israel to sin.

verses.rationale: Retains rampart from this pin rather than importing a plot of land.
verses.before: And concerning Jezebel the LORD also spoke, saying, ‘The dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.’
verses.after: The LORD also spoke about Jezebel: ‘Dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And concerning Jezebel the LORD also spoke, saying, ‘The dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated city/country judgment.
verses.before: Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the heavens will eat.”
verses.after: Dogs will eat anyone of Ahab’s house who dies in the city, and the birds of the sky will eat anyone who dies in the open country.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the heavens will eat.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Ahab’s agency alongside Jezebel’s instigation.
verses.before: Surely there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, whom Jezebel his wife incited.
verses.after: There was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the LORD’s eyes, urged on by his wife Jezebel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, whom Jezebel his wife incited.

verses.rationale: Retains the narrator’s comparison and displacement claim.
verses.before: He acted abominably by going after the idols, just as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the people of Israel.
verses.after: He acted most detestably in following idols, like everything the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: He acted abominably by going after the idols, just as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the people of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves all bodily acts without declaring inward motives.
verses.before: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his garments, put sackcloth on his body, and fasted. He lay in sackcloth and walked softly.
verses.after: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth against his skin, and fasted. He lay in sackcloth and walked about subdued.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his garments, put sackcloth on his body, and fasted. He lay in sackcloth and walked softly.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new response distinct from judgment.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains acknowledged humility and deferred, not canceled, judgment.
verses.before: “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the disaster upon his house.”
verses.after: “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself, I will not bring the disaster in his days. I will bring it on his house in his son’s days.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the disaster upon his house.”
